'''Sterling Beaumon''' <!-- Valid citation required for date of birth for BLP. (WP:BLPPRIVACY) --> is an American actor and producer. He is known for his roles as Max Doyle in the 2008 film, ''[[Mostly Ghostly (film)|Mostly Ghostly]]'', and as young [[Benjamin Linus]] in the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television series, ''[[Lost (2004 TV series)|Lost]]''. Beaumon has had guest roles in ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]'', ''[[Criminal Minds]]'', ''[[CSI: Crime Scene Investigation]]''. He has starred in series such as ''[[The Killing (American TV series)|The Killing]]'' and as "Seamus" on the television show ''[[Clue (miniseries)|Clue]]'', on [[The Hub (TV channel)|The Hub]] channel.<ref name=MOVIEWEB/>

==Career==
Beaumon guest-starred on an episode of the [[NBC]] series, ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]'',<ref name=MOVIEWEB>{{cite web|title=Sterling Beaumon: Credits|url=http://www.movieweb.com/person/sterling-beaumon/credits|access-date=5 March 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111208050011/http://www.movieweb.com/person/sterling-beaumon/credits|archive-date=8 December 2011}}</ref> as well as episodes of ''[[Bones (TV series)|Bones]]'', ''[[Scrubs (2001 TV series)|Scrubs]]'', ''[[Gary Unmarried]]'', ''[[Cold Case (TV series)|Cold Case]]'', and ''[[Crossing Jordan]]''.<ref name=MOVIEWEB/> He portrayed the young [[Benjamin Linus]] on the hit [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] series ''[[Lost (2004 TV series)|Lost]]''.<ref name=MOVIEWEB/>

He also appeared on the CBS series ''[[Criminal Minds]]'' in an episode entitled "Safe Haven." He followed that with work on the NBC series ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]''. His mother was portrayed by actress/producer [[Rita Wilson]].<ref name=TVGUIDE>{{cite web|title=TV Guide Credits|url=https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/sterling-beaumon/credits/271517|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928072234/http://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/sterling-beaumon/credits/271517|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 28, 2012|accessdate=5 March 2012}}</ref> He worked with [[Colin Firth]], [[Emily Blunt]], and [[Anne Heche]] in the 2012 film ''[[Arthur Newman (film)|Arthur Newman]]''.<ref name="Movie Web Golf Pro">{{cite web|url=http://www.movieweb.com/movie/arthur-newman-golf-pro/cast-crew|title=Movie Web: Golf Pro|access-date=February 22, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111208141528/http://www.movieweb.com/movie/arthur-newman-golf-pro/cast-crew|archive-date=December 8, 2011}}</ref>

Beaumon's [[voice-over]] work includes one of the English voices in the Japanese [[anime]] series ''[[Gun Sword|Gunsword]]'' and the [[Computer-generated imagery|CGI]] created ''[[Astro Boy (film)|Astro Boy]]''<ref name=TVGUIDE/> film. He was cast as Gabriel Walraven<ref name=RedWidowCast>{{cite web|title=Meet the Cast of Red Widow|url=http://beta.abc.go.com/shows/red-widow/blog/all/the-cast|access-date=16 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120621150954/http://beta.abc.go.com/shows/red-widow/blog/all/the-cast|archive-date=21 June 2012}}</ref> in the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] series ''[[Red Widow]]''.  The series aired between March and May 2013.<ref name=RedWiddowPremier>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=Upfront 2012: More Returning Than New Series With Shorter Orders This Year|url=https://deadline.com/2012/05/upfront-2012-more-returning-than-new-series-with-shorter-orders-this-year-273432/|access-date=16 July 2012}}</ref> In 2014, he portrayed Lincoln Knopf on the [[The Killing season 4|fourth and final season]] of the [[Netflix]] series, ''[[The Killing (American TV series)|The Killing]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url = https://deadline.com/2014/02/the-killing-adds-tyler-ross-sterling-beaumon-levi-meaden-677780/|title = The Killing Adds Tyler Ross, Sterling Beaumon, Levi Meaden|work = Deadline|access-date = 23 December 2014}}</ref>

'''David Uclés Vílchez''' ([[Úbeda]], 21 January 1990) is a Spanish writer, musician, illustrator, and translator. In 2024 he published ''La península de las casas vacías'' (The Peninsula of Empty Houses), which became a bestseller. In 2026 his novel ''La ciudad de las luces muertas'' (The City of Dead Lights) won the [[Nadal Prize]]. He is a Favorite Son of his birthplace.

== Biography ==
David Uclés studied [[linguistics]] in Córdoba, Münster (Germany), and Granada, and worked as a teacher of Spanish, German, and English in Germany, France, and Switzerland. He also lived in England and spent several years in Galicia,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-23 |title=David Uclés, el autor andaluz de uno de los libros del año que siempre vuelve en verano a Santiago y ahora sorprende tocando la campana de la Catedral |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/santiago/vivir-santiago/2024/07/23/david-ucles-autor-andaluz-libros-ano-siempre-vuelve-verano-santiago-sorprende-tocando-campana-catedral/00031721736596394559585.htm |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=La Voz de Galicia |language=es}}</ref> the Basque Country, and Catalonia. He currently resides in Madrid.<ref name="academia" />

His work fall within the literary movement of [[magical realism]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martínez |first=Borja |date=2026-01-08 |title=El realismo mágico ataca Barcelona |url=https://www.elindependiente.com/opinion/2026/01/08/el-realismo-magico-ataca-barcelona/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=El Independiente |language=es}}</ref> and among his literary influences are [[Günter Grass]], [[Gabriel García Márquez]], [[José Saramago]], [[Mercè Rodoreda]], [[Miguel de Unamuno]], [[Salman Rushdie]], [[Edgar Hilsenrath]], and [[Olga Tokarczuk]].

In 2019, he received the Complutense Prize for Literature in the narrative category for his first work, ''El llanto del león'',<ref name="complutense">{{Cite web |title=Tribuna Complutense :: UCM |url=https://www.ucm.es/tribunacomplutense/246/art3677.php |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=www.ucm.es}}</ref> a theatrical novel that recounts the last conversations between a father suffering from cancer and his ten-year-old son. The president of the jury was [[Luis Mateo Díez]], winner of the 2023 [[Cervantes Prize]]. In 2020, he published ''Emilio & Octubre'' with the Dos Bigotes publishing house, a novel that tells the love story of two men from the birth of one to the death of the other, in the near future, in which the protagonists enter three-dimensional paintings in museums and travel through art across Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madrid |first=Carlos |date=2025-06-06 |title=David Uclés y 'Emilio y Octubre': la historia de un amor platónico que sucede dentro de sus cuadros favoritos |url=https://www.traveler.es/articulos/david-ucles-y-emilio-y-octubre-la-historia-de-un-amor-platonico-que-sucede-dentro-de-sus-cuadros-favoritos |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=Traveler |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=David Uclés y la novela del amor homosexual puro |url=https://lacontradejaen.eldiario.es/ucles-ubeda-novela-jaen/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=lacontradejaen.eldiario.es |language=es}}</ref>

His third novel, ''La península de las casas vacías'', published by Ediciones Siruela in March 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Babelia |date=2024-04-22 |title=Las 30 recomendaciones de ‘Babelia’ para el Día del Libro de 2024 |url=https://elpais.com/babelia/2024-04-22/las-30-recomendaciones-de-babelia-para-el-dia-del-libro-de-2024.html |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=El País |language=es}}</ref> narrates the entire [[Spanish Civil War]] in a [[Magical realism|magical realist]] style. It is the result of fifteen years of work and an exhaustive journey of documentation and memory throughout Spain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gómez |first=Nel |date=2026-01-07 |title=El duro camino de David Uclés hasta el éxito de 'La península de las casas vacías' y el Premio Nadal: “Nunca había tenido más de 500 euros en el banco” |url=https://www.infobae.com/espana/cultura/2026/01/07/el-duro-camino-de-david-ucles-hasta-el-exito-de-la-peninsula-de-las-casas-vacias-y-el-premio-nadal-nunca-habia-tenido-mas-de-500-euros-en-el-banco/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref> For its creation, it received the Montserrat Roig and Leonardo scholarships.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morán |first=David |date=2026-01-11 |title=El 'efecto Uclés': las becas y residencias literarias como 'armadura' económica y creativa |url=https://www.elperiodico.com/es/ocio-y-cultura/20260111/efecto-ucles-becas-residencias-literarias-125484297 |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=El Periódico |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=David Uclés Vílchez, becario Leonardo 2022 en Creación Literaria |url=https://www.redleonardo.es/beneficiario/david-ucles/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=Red Leonardo |language=es}}</ref><ref name="academia">{{Cite web |title=Uclés, David |url=https://academialacentral.com/profesor/250 |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=academialacentral.com}}</ref>

It was awarded the Cálamo Best Book of the Year Award 2024,<ref name="calamo">{{Cite web  |date=2025-01-13 |title='La península de las casas vacías', de David Uclés, elegido Libro del año 2024 en los Premios Cálamo |url=https://www.europapress.es/aragon/noticia-peninsula-casas-vacias-david-ucles-elegido-libro-ano-2024-premios-calamo-20250113125707.html |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=www.europapress.es}}</ref> the Andalusia Critics' Award 2025, the Espartaco Award from the Semana Negra de Gijón for Best Historical Novel, the Kelvin 505 Award for Best Fantasy Novel, the Dulce Chacón Award 2025, the Arcebispo Juan de San Clemente Literary Prize, the Festival 42 Prize for Best Novel in Spanish, the Andalucía de las Letras 2025, the El Corte Inglés Un Año de Libros 2025 Prize for Best Fiction Book, and was a finalist for the VI Mario Vargas Llosa Biennial Novel Prize. It was also the Spanish candidate for the 2025 European Union Prize for Literature. It reached 30 editions in less than two years and sold over 300,000 copies, becoming one of the best-selling books of 2024 and 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-23 |title=Blackwater, Joana Marcús y David Uclés: bestsellers bien |url=https://www.eldiario.es/carnecruda/programas/blackwater-joana-marcus-david-ucles-bestsellers_132_11757813.html |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=elDiario.es |language=es}}</ref> The novel is being translated into 15 languages, including French, Portuguese, German, Italian, Danish, Lithuanian, Romanian, Czech, Galician, Albanian, Serbian, and Greek. It was selected as the second-best book of the year by the jury of Babelia's annual list (2024).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Babelia |date=2024-12-14 |title=Los 50 mejores libros de 2024 |url=https://elpais.com/babelia/2024-12-14/los-50-mejores-libros-de-2024.html |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=El País |language=es}}</ref>

In February 2026, he published his fourth novel, ''La ciudad de las luces muertas'' (The City of Dead Lights), which recreates a dark Barcelona through which a hundred artists and writers from different eras pass, all maintaining a relationship with the city. The literary project was begun in 2021 and uses the writer [[Carmen Laforet]] as a central figure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-04 |title=David Uclés publica 'La ciudad de las luces muertas': "La esperanza tienes que crearla" |url=https://www.europapress.es/catalunya/noticia-david-ucles-publica-ciudad-luces-muertas-esperanza-tienes-crearla-20260204164834.html |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=www.europapress.es}}</ref> The novel won the [[Nadal Prize]], submitted under the pseudonym Oriol Arce and the title ''Ruge otro día estival'' (Another Summer Day Roars). Uclés dedicated the literary award to the writers [[Mercè Rodoreda]], [[Montserrat Roig]], and Laforet.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=David Uclés gana el Premio Nadal con la novela 'La ciudad de las luces muertas' |url=https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20260106/david-ucles-gana-premio-nadal/16884230.shtml |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=RTVE.es |language=es}}</ref>

In addition, David Uclés has been named Favorite Son of Úbeda by the City Council of Úbeda<ref>{{Cite web |title=Así fue el nombramiento de David Uclés, Zahara y Moisés Nieto como Hijos Predilectos de Úbeda |url=https://www.diariojaen.es/provincia/asi-fue-el-nombramiento-de-david-ucles-zahara-y-moises-nieto-como-hijos-predilectos-de-ubeda-GG11066312 |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=www.diariojaen.es |language=es}}</ref> and has won the Jaén Paraíso Interior Award granted by the Provincial Council of Jaén.<ref>{{Cite web |title=David Uclés, distinguido en los Premios Jaén, paraíso interior 2025 |url=https://www.diariojaen.es/provincia/david-ucles-distinguido-en-los-premios-jaen-paraiso-interior-2025-HP10869619 |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=www.diariojaen.es |language=es-ES}}</ref>

As a musician, he sings and composes on the harp, piano, accordion, and guitar. He has composed the music for various plays, documentaries, and exhibitions (Tabacalera,<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.rtve.es/play/videos/pagina-dos/pagina-dos-losotros-14may/3610725/ |title=Página Dos - Programa cultural en RTVE Play |date=2016-05-17 |language=es |access-date=2026-04-26 |via=www.rtve.es}}</ref> University of Paris,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-10-12 |title=From one world to another / D'un monde à l'autre |url=https://kfruchtnis.wordpress.com/2013/10/12/from-one-world-to-another-dun-monde-a-lautre/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=K L A U S   F R U C H T N I S |language=en}}</ref> [[LesGaiCineMad]]).

'''Janani Krishnan-Jha''' (October 5, 1998), formerly known by the stage name '''J. Maya''', is an American singer-songwriter. In 2023 she participated in ''[[Survivor 45]]'', the 45th season of the American reality-TV competition series ''[[Survivor (American TV series)|Survivor]]''. The release of her debut single in 2021, "Achilles Heel", influenced by [[Greco-Roman mythology]], garnered streams. Her debut [[Extended play|EP]], ''Poetic License'', received positive reviews from media outlets in 2022. In 2024, she released her debut album, ''The Rest of the Laurels'', with an accompanying novella ''Katathon''.

==Early life and education==
Krishnan-Jha was born in the United States to [[Indian people|Indian]] [[Tamil people|Tamil]] parents.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Janani K. Jha on TikTok: As a Tamil woman writing music inspired by literary classics, this feels like a dream come true 📚💛|url=https://www.tiktok.com/@jananikjha/video/7080675877822025003 |date=March 30, 2022 |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=TikTok}}</ref> She grew up in the [[San Francisco Bay Area]], where she attended [[San Mateo High School]]. There, she was captain of the Mock Trial Team, president of the [[Model UN]], founder and president of the Speech & Debate Club, president/student director of the choir, executive member of the Renaissance Leadership Team, and publicity chair of the Writing Club. In 2015, she received the National Scholastic Award in Writing, which she accepted at [[Carnegie Hall]]. She also worked as an intern for [[United States House of Representatives]] member [[Jackie Speier]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]-[[California|CA]]) while attending high school.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.shcp.edu/news/tedxyouthshc-speakers-announced-2016 | title=TEDxYouth@SHC Speakers Announced! | publisher=[[Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory]] | date=March 29, 2016 | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | author=Chu, Thai}}</ref>

In 2016, Krishnan-Jha competed in the [[O. Henry Pun-Off|O. Henry Pun-Off World Championships]] in [[Austin, Texas]]. She was named MVP (Most Valuable Punster) of the competition.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://texashighways.com/culture/pun-pun-pun/ | title=Pun, Pun, Pun | publisher=[[Texas Department of Transportation]] | magazine=[[Texas Highways]] | date=April 17, 2017 | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | author=Held, Joey}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, she began attending [[Harvard University]], where she served as a public service student representative for the [[Dunster House]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://publicservice.fas.harvard.edu/people/janani-krishnan-jha | title=Janani Krishnan-Jha | publisher=The President and Fellows of Harvard College | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | website=[[Harvard University]]}} </ref> for which she sang Claire Fridkin's parody of [[Juice (Lizzo song)]], "Moose!"<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4itZalWyH70 | title=Moose - Dunster Housing Day 2020 | publisher=Dunster House|website=YouTube}}</ref> During her time at Harvard, Krishnan-Jha also participated in the [[The Harvard-Radcliffe Veritones]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BKL2IsZD0Yj/ | title=Meet Isaiah, Isabella and Janani, the newest members of our family! | publisher=[[The Harvard-Radcliffe Veritones]] | website=Instagram}}</ref> where she had a solo cover recording of [[Troye Sivan]]'s EASE.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BNsrNFvDx85/ | title=Need a study break? | website=Instagram | author=[[The Harvard-Radcliffe Veritones]]}}</ref> She graduated in 2020 with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] ''cum laude'' in psychology.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.backstage.com/u/jananikjha/ | title=Janani Krishnan-Jha | publisher=Backstage | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | website=Backstage.com}}</ref> She stated in 2023 that she had been accepted into [[Harvard Law School]], but turned the offer down to concentrate on her singing career.<ref name="ew">{{cite magazine | url=https://ew.com/tv/survivor-45-cast-photos-bios-revealed/ | title=Meet the cast of ''Survivor 45'' | publisher=[[Dotdash Meredith]] | magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] | date=September 6, 2023 | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | author=Ross, Dalton}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2021, Krishnan-Jha released her first single, "Achilles Heel", which received more than 150,000 streams across platforms in the first three days of its release.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://booksnbackpacks.com/achilles-heel/ | title=Achilles Heel: Enjoy Myths in J. Maya's New Single | date=December 8, 2021 | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | author=Livia | website=Books 'n' Backpacks}}</ref> She released the single under the pseudonym '''J. Maya''' in which the letter "J" is the initial for her first name "Janani" and "[[Maya (given name)|Maya]]" in Sanskrit means "illusion or magic" as music to her was "100% fantasy, my escape".<ref name="stage name">{{cite AV media |date=August 24, 2024 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1rgeTxoNRMQ |title=Why I'm changing my artist name from J. Maya to my birth name! ❤️ |publisher=Janani K. Jha |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=April 5, 2025}}</ref>

J. Maya's first [[Extended play|EP]], ''Poetic License'', was released in 2022. The EP spawned four singles: "Library Card", "Sunday Crossword", "Machine Learning", and "Three Specters."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://open.spotify.com/artist/6uFYqDeLIwfURuF1yxVqJU/discography | title=J. Maya – Discography | publisher=Spotify AB | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | website=Spotify}}</ref> ''Poetic License'', as well as Krishnan-Jha's songwriting at large, has been recognized by media outlets like [[NME]],<ref>{{cite web |title=The NME 100: essential emerging artists for 2023 |url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-radar/the-nme-100-essential-emerging-artists-for-2023-radar-3372061 |website=NME |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref> [[Good Morning America]],<ref>{{cite web |title=From 'super nerd' to superstar: Youngest pun champion writes punny pop songs l GMA |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=npiC6SSp9Kk |website=YouTube |publisher=Good Morning America |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref> Uproxx,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lane |first1=Lexi |title=All The Best New Pop Music From This Week |url=https://uproxx.com/pop/best-new-pop-pinkpantheress-rm-troye-sivan-noah-cyrus/ |website=Uproxx |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref> VOGUE India,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rao |first1=Pritikia |title=J. Maya is the MVP: Most Valuable Punner |url=https://www.vogue.in/content/indian-american-singer-songwriter-j-maya-is-the-mvp-most-valuable-punner |website=VOGUE India |publisher=VOGUE |access-date=12 September 2024}}</ref> Forbes,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kim |first1=Regina |title=AAPI Artists To Watch: Iam Tongi, Emei, Eric Nam, Lyn Lapid And More |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/reginakim/2024/06/27/aapi-artists-to-watch-iam-tongi-emei-eric-nam-lyn-lapid-and-more/ |work=Forbes |access-date=12 September 2024}}</ref> and Coup de Main,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jacob |first1=Lola |title=Introducing: J. Maya and her upcoming 'Poectic Licence' EP. |journal=Coup de Main |date=November 28, 2022 |url=https://www.coupdemainmagazine.com/j-maya/18914}}</ref> and music institutions such as [[The Recording Academy]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Chloe |title=TikTok's Musical Class Of 2022: 12 Singer/Songwriters Who Went From Viral Stars To Hit-Making Artists, From Jax To Nicky Youre |url=https://www.grammy.com/news/tiktok-songs-2022-artists-singer-songwriters-music-trends-victorias-secret-billie-eilish-sunroof-fingers-crossed-snap-numb-little-bug |website=Grammy Awards |publisher=Recording Academy |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>

In 2023, Jha (under the name J. Maya) was one of 18 participants in ''[[Survivor 45]]'', the 45th season of ''[[Survivor (American TV series)|Survivor]]''.<ref name="ew" /> She was voted out in the sixth episode, placing 13th and missing out on the jury.<ref>{{Cite magazine |author=Ross, Dalton |date=November 2, 2023 |title=''Survivor 45'' star J Maya reacts to being called out by Kaleb at Tribal Council |url=https://ew.com/tv/survivor-45-j-maya-interview/ |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |publisher=[[Dotdash Meredith]] |accessdate=November 3, 2023}}</ref> This opportunity greatly boosted Jha's streaming numbers on Spotify and drew eyes to her creative work.<ref>{{cite web |title=Janani K. Jha Spotify Analytics |url=https://songstats.com/artist/150wvb2a/janani-k-jha?source=spotify |website=Songstats |publisher=Songstats}}</ref>

In 2024, she dropped her stage name as she "wanted to bring a little bit of [herself]" into music.<ref name="stage name" /> Under the name Janani K. Jha, she released her debut album, ''The Rest of the Laurels'', a concept album inspired by Greco-Roman mythology, with each track representing a myth. ''The Rest of the Laurels'' peaked at #67 on the [[iTunes]] U.S. pop and pop charts. It peaked at #26 on the Canadian pop chart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Never in my wildest dreams did I think that something like this would be possible |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@jananikjha/video/7446273114385681707?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc |website=TikTok}}</ref> Alongside this album, she wrote a companion novella, ''Katathon'', which describes the nine levels of Hell noted in [[Dante's Inferno]] through the eyes of a modern-day [[Eurydice]] going through the dimension as part of a competition. Each chapter in ''Katathon'' is named after and is linked to a song in ''The Rest of the Laurels.''<ref>{{cite web |title=Katathon: The Official Companion Novella to The Rest of the Laurels |url=https://www.amazon.com/Katathon-Official-Companion-Novella-Laurels-ebook/dp/B0DM1TVR3H |website=Amazon |publisher=Amazon}}</ref> ''Katathon'' peaked at #1 on [[Amazon Books]]' Greek Mythology Retellings for Young Adults Bestselling Chart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Janani K. Jha Official Website, About |url=http://jananikjha.com/about |website=Janani K. Jha Official Site}}</ref>

On June 30, 2025, Krishnan-Jha's song ''Slow Burn'' was featured on Season 7, Episode 25 of [[Love Island]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Love Island (US) Soundtrack |url=https://www.tunefind.com/show/love-island-us/season-7/265247 |website=Tunefind}}</ref> Following, the song found new heights of notice on social media platforms such as TikTok and Reddit, causing streaming numbers to skyrocket.

== Musical style and influences ==
Krishnan-Jha cites [[Western literature]] and [[Greco-Roman mythology]] as influences on her music.<ref name="new9">{{cite web | url=https://thenewnine.com/artist-to-watch-j-mayas-poetic-license/ | title=Artist To Watch: J. Maya's Poetic License | work=The New Nine | date=January 11, 2023 | accessdate=November 2, 2023 | author=Treadgold, Emily}}</ref> She also lists pop artists [[Ariana Grande]], [[Beyoncé]], [[Katy Perry]], and [[Taylor Swift]] as her favorite musical influences.<ref name="coup">{{cite magazine |author=Jacob, Lola |date=November 23, 2022 |title=Introducing: J. Maya and her upcoming 'Poectic Licence' (sic) EP. |url=https://www.coupdemainmagazine.com/j-maya/18914 |magazine=Coup de Main |accessdate=November 2, 2023}}</ref> Her musical style mixes elements of jazz with [[South India]]n [[Carnatic music]].<ref name="new9" />

[[Royal College of Art]] | occupation = Artist, composer, poet, writer | known_for = [[Painting]], [[poetry]], [[sound art]] | awards = | website = {{URL|jetleparti.com}} }} '''Jet Le Parti''' (born July 9 1998, [[Columbus, Georgia]]) is an American artist, musician, poet, and writer. He is the founder of Base 36 , an art gallery, cultural research platform and record label based in [[Brooklyn]], New York, and Sibyl, a private collection and advisory based in Los Angeles. ==Early life and education== Le Parti was born in [[Columbus, Georgia]], on July 9, 1998 and grew up on [[Fort Benning]], a U.S. Army post near the city. He played baseball as a teenager, was named a Preseason All-American by the scouting organization Perfect Game USA, and entered the [[University of Pennsylvania]] as a recruited athlete.{{cite web |title=Jet Le Parti Class of 2017 - Player Profile |url=https://www.perfectgame.org/players/playerprofile.aspx?ID=409984 |website=Perfect Game |access-date=November 18, 2023}} Le Parti attended the University of Pennsylvania to study [[philosophy]] and [[cognitive neuroscience]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.34st.com/article/2020/02/jet-le-parti-philosophy-artist-apartment-studio-taking-flight|title=Meet Jet Le Parti, The Self–Taught Artist Who Turned his Apartment into a Studio|website=www.34st.com|access-date=November 18, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Les Nouveaux Riches Magazine – Self-taught artist. Jet Le Parti |url=https://www.les-nouveaux-riches.com/self-taught-artist-jet-le-parti/ |date=April 21, 2020 |access-date=November 18, 2023|website=}} He later attended the [[Royal College of Art]].{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Entrepreneur Middle East |date=2026-01-25 |title=The Linen Road |url=https://mena.entrepreneur.com/lifestyle/the-linen-road/502251 |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=Entrepreneur Middle East |language=en-US}} His academic background and interest in [[Phenomenology (philosophy)|phenomenology]], critical theory, and [[physics]] have informed his multidisciplinary approach, combining conceptual frameworks with sensory experimentation.{{Cite web|url=https://officemagazine.net/down-rabbit-hole-jet-le-parti|title=Down the Rabbit Hole with Jet Le Parti|date=October 29, 2021|website=Office Magazine|access-date=November 18, 2023}} ==Career== === Visual art === [[File:Jet Le Parti - Trojan (2023), RP.1 New York.jpg|thumb|''Trojan'' (2023), RP.1, Chinatown, New York. Courtesy of Base 36.|251x251px]]Le Parti is a self-taught multimedia experimental artist.{{Cite web |title=Jet Le Parti. American, b. 1998 |url=https://www.artsy.net/artist/jet-le-parti |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=Artsy |language=en}} His paintings use house paint, graphite, ink, aerosol, oil, and wax. His subjects have included mortality, systemic violence, cultural saturation, and observation, and his output is organized into bodies of work. The ''Melting Blues'' series consists of paintings in muted blue and grey palettes.{{Cite web |date=2023-01-11 |title=Inching Towards the End of the World with Jet Le Parti |url=https://hypebeast.com/2023/1/inching-towards-the-end-of-the-world-with-jet-le-parti |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=Hypebeast |language=en}} ''Reign.925'', produced with the artist L.S. Toy, combines graffiti, stencil, silkscreen, plaster, acrylic transfers, and photography with painting.{{Cite web |last=Coffey-Behrens |first=Kelly |date=2026-04-28 |title=Indie Film Breaks The System With ‘Underground’ Launch |url=https://theblast.com/799101/indie-film-breaks-system-underground-launch/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=The Blast |language=en-US}} Le Parti does not have gallery representation and has declined sales, collaborations, and formal showings; his work has traded on the secondary market.{{cite web |title=Beyond the Auction Block: How the Art Market Values What It Cannot See |url=https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/beyond-the-auction-block-how-the-art-market-values-what-it-cannot-see/ |website=Global Banking & Finance Review |date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=2026-04-21}} Individual works include ''To Be Hung'' (2022)'', Trojan'' (2023)'', Window, Face in Cave'', ''Portrait of a YN'' (2026), ''2 Avant Garde Noise Listeners'' (2026), and ''Revenant / Walker in the District'' (2026). Earlier paintings, including ''History of the World'', ''Pandora/Prometheus'', and ''On Phenomenology'', are held at Sibyl in Los Angeles.{{cite web |title=By Any Means Necessary: Origins of Base 36 |url=https://whitehotmagazine.com/articles/means-necessary-origins-base-36/6668 |website=Whitehot Magazine of Contemporary Art |author=Jeffrey Grunthaner |date=November 22, 2024 |access-date=2026-04-21}}[[File:Jet Le Parti - Revenant, Walker in the District (2026).jpg|thumb|''Revenant / Walker in the District'' (2026). Courtesy of Sibyl.|200x200px]][[File:Jet Le Parti working in studio - 2021.jpg|thumb|Le Parti at his Brooklyn studio, 2021. Courtesy of Base 36.|253x253px]] ===Music=== Le Parti produces [[Experimental music|experimental]] sound and electronic music under his own name. His works combine [[Ambient music|ambient]], [[Drone music|drone]], [[minimal techno]], and [[spoken word]] elements, and has performed as a [[disc jockey|DJ]] in warehouse and club settings.{{cite web |title=Inside American Wasteland: When Hollywood Independence Collided with the New York Underground |url=https://relaispunkt.one |website=RP.1 |date=2026}}{{cite web |title=Jet Le Parti · Artist Profile |url=https://ra.co/dj/jetleparti |website=Resident Advisor |access-date=November 18, 2023}}{{Cite web|url=https://edmtrain.com/tours/jet-le-parti-26347|title=Jet Le Parti Tour|website=Edmtrain|access-date=November 18, 2023}} His 2026 album ''Listening Post'' was released through RP.1, the label and gallery division of Base 36. Reviewers have compared the album to the work of Scanner, [[William Basinski]], and [[Tim Hecker]], alongside Japanese electronic musicians Shinichi Atobe, Takaaki Itoh, Wata Igarashi, [[Merzbow]], and [[Susumu Yokota]].{{cite web |title=Interview & Column: From the Front Lines -- Jet Le Parti's "Listening Post" |url=https://www.billboard-japan.com/d_news/detail/159835/2 |website=Billboard Japan |date=March 31, 2026 |access-date=March 31, 2026 |lang=ja}} === Writing === Le Parti's work includes poetry collections and cultural essays. His poetry focuses on the existential and philosophical themes that are also present in his visual art. His poetry collection ''every day is a countdown'' includes short poems such as ''Skin'', ''Weekend'', ''Teeth, and Countdown'' and longer poems including ''Fruits of the Loom I'' and ''II'', ''Bits & Pieces'', ''Airport Orders'', and ''Ramble''.{{cite web |title=Jet Le Parti and the Poetry of the Impossible Middle Ground |url=https://www.villagevoice.com/jet-le-parti-and-the-poetry-of-the-impossible-middle-ground/ |website=The Village Voice |author=Will Jones |date=April 14, 2026 |access-date=April 14, 2026}} His essays on culture and philosophy include ''Errors & Residuals'' (2021), ''Residuum: On the Phenomenology of Saturation and the Aesthetics of Afterwards'' (2025)  and ''Hide & Seek: Theory & Action'' (2026).{{cite web |title=Without a Trace! {{Short description|Brazilian rally-raid driver}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2025}} {{Infobox racing driver |name=Lucas Moraes |image= |image_size= |alt= |caption= |nationality={{flagicon|BRA}} Brazilian |birth_date={{birth date and age|1989|12|12|df=yes}} |birth_place=[[São Paulo]], Brazil |relatives= |current_team=[[Automobile Dacia|Dacia Sandriders]] }} '''Lucas Moraes''' (born 12 December 1989){{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/motor/noticia/2025/09/28/brasileiro-lucas-moraes-e-campeao-do-rally-de-portugal.ghtml|title=Brasileiro Lucas Moraes é campeão do Rally de Portugal|website=[[Globo.com]]|language=pt|date=28 September 2025|access-date=18 October 2025}} is a Brazilian [[off-road racing]] driver. He is currently driving for [[Automobile Dacia|Dacia Sandriders]] in the [[2026 World Rally-Raid Championship|World Rally-Raid Championship]] as part of [[Red Bull]]'s rallying team for [[rally raid]] events. Moraes has achieved multiple accolades throughout his career, including winning the South American Mitsubishi Cup on two occasions, the Brazilian championship three times, as well as finishing third on his [[2023 Dakar Rally|Dakar Rally]] debut in 2023.{{Cite web |title=Lucas Moraes |url=https://www.redbull.com/int-en/athlete/lucas-moraes |access-date=2024-01-14 |website=Red Bull |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Profile of LUCAS MORAES - TOYOTA GAZOO RACING - Dakar |url=https://www.dakar.com/en/competitor/203 |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=www.dakar.com |language=en}} After culminating a three-year stint at [[Toyota Gazoo Racing|Toyota]] with a [[World Rally-Raid Championship|W2RC]] title in 2025, he moved to [[Automobile Dacia|Dacia]].{{cite web|url=https://dirtfish.com/off-road/dakar/world-rally-raid-champion-leaves-toyota-for-dacia/|title=World Rally-Raid champion leaves Toyota for Dacia|website=DirtFish|last=Barry|first=Luke|date=21 October 2025|access-date=13 April 2026}} == W2RC career == In his first attempt at the Dakar Rally in [[2023 Dakar Rally|2023]], Moraes drove a Toyota for Overdrive Racing. Partnering experienced co-driver [[Timo Gottschalk]], Moraes became a surprise frontrunner by the end of the first week, sitting third overall after the first six stages.{{Cite web |title=Dakar-Beifahrer Timo Gottschalk Dritter: "Wir sind hungrig auf das Podium" |url=https://www.motorsport-total.com/dakar/news/dakar-beifahrer-timo-gottschalk-dritter-wir-sind-hungrig-auf-das-podium-23010701 |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=Motorsport-Total.com |language=de}} {{short description|American professional golfer (born 1999)}} {{Use American English|date=April 2026}} {{use mdy dates|date=May 2024}} {{Infobox golfer | name = Chris Gotterup | image = | image_size = | caption = | full_name = Christopher Gotterup | nickname = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1999|7|20}} | birth_place = [[Easton, Maryland]], U.S. | death_date = | death_place = | height = 6 ft 0 in | weight = 210 lb | sporting_nationality = {{USA}} | residence = [[Edmond, Oklahoma]], U.S. | spouse = | partner = | children = | college = [[Rutgers University]]
[[University of Oklahoma]] | status = | yearpro = 2022 | tour = [[PGA Tour]] | extour = [[Korn Ferry Tour]] | prowins = 6 | pgawins = 5 | eurowins = 1 | japwins = | asiawins = | sunwins = | auswins = | nwidewins = | chalwins = | livwins = | champwins = | seneurowins = | otherwins = 1 | majorwins = | masters = T24: 2026 | pga = T10: [[2026 PGA Championship|2026]] | usopen = T23: 2025 | open = 3rd: [[2025 Open Championship|2025]] | wghofid = | wghofyear = | award1 = [[Haskins Award]] | year1 = 2022 | award2 = Jack Nicklaus Award | year2 = 2022 | awardssection = | show-medals = | medaltemplates = }} '''Christopher Gotterup''' (born July 20, 1999) is an American [[professional golfer]] who plays on the [[PGA Tour]], where he has won five times. ==Early life and amateur career== Gotterup was born in [[Easton, Maryland]], to Kate and Morten Gotterup. He has a brother named Patrick and a sister named Anna, and was raised in [[Little Silver, New Jersey]].{{Cite web |title=Chris Gotterup |url=https://www.pgatour.com/player/59095/chris-gotterup/bio |access-date=2025-07-20 |publisher=PGA Tour}}{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title=Little Silver's Gotterup Wins First PGA Tour Title in 27th Start |newspaper=Two River Times |url=https://tworivertimes.com/gotterupwinsfirstpgatourtitle/ |access-date=2025-07-29}} He is of [[Danish Americans|Danish descent]] through his paternal grandparents, who were born in Denmark. His father speaks Danish, but he does not.{{Cite news |date=2025-07-20 |title=Gotterup inspired by European blood to finish third in Open |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/golf/gotterup-inspired-by-european-blood-finish-third-open-2025-07-20/ |access-date=2025-07-29 |work=Reuters}}{{Cite web |last=Zgoda |first=Jerry |date=2025-07-26 |title=Thorbjørn Olesen joins a Danish uprising, seizing the lead at the 3M Open |url=https://www.startribune.com/3m-open-tpc-twin-cities-blaine-mn-pga-tour-thorbjorn-oleson-jake-knapp/601390721 |access-date=2025-07-29 |newspaper=Star Tribune}} As of 2025, Gotterup uses the Danish spelling of his name, Gøtterup, on his Instagram profile.{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/chrisgotterup/ |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=www.instagram.com}} Gotterup's father was a collegiate tennis player and an accomplished golfer, who won multiple New Jersey State Golf Association tournaments.{{Cite web |title=New Jersey Native Chris Gotterup Returns Home for a New Korn Ferry Tour Event |url=https://magnitchampionship.com/news/new-jersey-native-chris-gotterup-returns-home-for-a-new-korn-ferry-tour-event |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=magnitchampionship.com}} Gotterup played varsity golf at [[Christian Brothers Academy (New Jersey)|Christian Brothers Academy]] in nearby [[Lincroft, New Jersey|Lincroft]] and graduated in 2017.{{cite web |last=Edelson |first=Stephen |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/2025/07/13/legendary-jersey-shore-golf-coach-reacts-to-chris-gotterup-victory/85037629007/ |title='It was spectacular': Legendary Shore golf coach reacts to Chris Gotterup winning Scottish Open |website=app.com |date=July 13, 2025 |access-date=July 18, 2025}} Gotterup stayed in New Jersey and played college golf at [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers University]] from 2017 to 2021.{{cite web |url=https://scarletknights.com/sports/mens-golf/roster/christopher-gotterup/7869 |title=Christopher Gotterup |publisher=Rutgers University Athletics}} Gotterup became one of the greatest college golfers in the nation and was one of the greatest in Scarlet Knights history. When he graduated, he held school records in scoring average, par 3 scoring, par 4 scoring, par 5 scoring, and number of par or better rounds. Gotterup received the following accolades in his time at Rutgers:{{Cite web |date=2026-03-10 |title=Christopher Gotterup - Men's Golf |url=https://scarletknights.com/sports/mens-golf/roster/christopher-gotterup/7869 |access-date=2026-03-25 |publisher=Rutgers University Athletics}} * 2019–20 Big Ten Player of the Year * 2020 First Team All-Big Ten * 2019–20 Big Ten Les Bolstad Award (lowest conference stroke average) * 2020 NCAA Division I PING All-American (Third Team) * 2020 GolfWeek All-American (Honorable Mention) In 2019, he won the [[Metropolitan Amateur]] and [[New Jersey State Open]], and was given the Metropolitan Golf Association Jerry Courville Sr. Player of the Year Award.{{cite web |url=https://mgahonors.org/honorees/christopher-gotterup-2019/ |title=Christopher Gotterup (2019) |publisher=Metropolitan Golf Association}} Gotterup transferred to the [[Oklahoma Sooners|University of Oklahoma]] for 2021–22, where he won the [[Haskins Award]] and Jack Nicklaus [[List of golf awards#Intercollegiate golf|Award]] as the top college golfer.{{cite web |url=https://soonersports.com/sports/mens-golf/roster/chris-gotterup/14800 |title=Chris Gotterup |publisher=University of Oklahoma Athletics}} ==Professional career== Gotterup turned professional in 2022 after the NCAA championship. He played events on both the [[PGA Tour]] and [[Korn Ferry Tour]] in 2022 including a T-4 finish at the [[John Deere Classic]].{{cite web |url=https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/needtoknow/2022/07/03/five-things-to-know-christopher-gotterup-john-deere-classic-barbasol-championship-oklahoma-university |title=Five Things to Know: Christopher Gotterup |publisher=PGA Tour |first=Sean |last=Martin |date=July 3, 2022}} He finished T-3 at the Korn Ferry Tour Q-School to earn his 2023 Korn Ferry Tour card.{{cite web |url=https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/university/2022/11/07/pga-tour-university-on-tour-chris-gotterup-finishes-t3-korn-ferry-tour-q-school-finals |title=PGA Tour University On Tour: Chris Gotterup finishes T3 Korn Ferry Tour Q-School Finals |publisher=PGA Tour |date=November 7, 2022}} He had three top-10 finishes on the tour in 2023 and earned his 2024 PGA Tour card by finishing 23rd on the [[2023 Korn Ferry Tour graduates|Korn Ferry Tour points list]]. On May 12, 2024, he won the [[Myrtle Beach Classic]] for his first PGA Tour victory.{{cite web |title=Chris Gotterup wins Myrtle Beach Classic for first PGA Tour title |url=https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/daily-wrapup/2024/05/12/chris-gotterup-wins-myrtle-beach-classic-for-first-pga-tour-title |publisher=PGA Tour |agency=Associated Press |date=May 12, 2024 |access-date=May 21, 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2024/5/13/former-ru-mens-golfer-chris-gotterup-wins-1st-pga-tour-event-at-myrtle-beach.aspx |title=Chris Gotterup Wins 1st PGA Tour Event at Myrtle Beach Classic |publisher=Rutgers University Athletics |first=Chris |last=Corso |date=May 13, 2024}} In July 2025, Gotterup won the [[Genesis Scottish Open]] by two shots over [[Rory McIlroy]] and [[Marco Penge]]. It was his first win in a [[DP World Tour]] event and second PGA Tour victory.{{cite news |last=Ritchie |first=Cameron |title=Genesis Scottish Open: Chris Gotterup crowned 2025 champion |url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/news/25310410.genesis-scottish-open-chris-gotterup-crowned-2025-champion/ |newspaper=East Lothian Courier |access-date=13 July 2025 |date=13 July 2025}}{{cite news |last=Watt |first=Martin |title=Gotterup 'hung in like champ' to deny McIlroy at Scottish Open |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/golf/articles/c2d08w1yej2o |work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 July 2025 |date=13 July 2025}} He followed that up the next week with a solo 3rd finish at the [[2025 Open Championship]]. In January 2026, Gotterup won the season opening [[Sony Open in Hawaii]] by two strokes over [[Ryan Gerard]].{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/golf/story?id=47656580&_slug_=chris-gotterup-opens-pga-tour-season-winning-sony-open |title=Chris Gotterup opens PGA Tour season by winning Sony Open |work=ESPN |date=January 18, 2026}} Three weeks later, he won the [[WM Phoenix Open]] in a sudden-death playoff over [[Hideki Matsuyama]].{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/golf/story/_/id/47871400/chris-gotterup-wins-phoenix-open-first-playoff-hole-hideki-matsuyama-falters |title=Gotterup wins Phoenix Open in playoff as Matsuyama falters |work=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=February 8, 2026}} He jumped to 5th in the [[Official World Golf Ranking]], his best position.{{cite magazine |url=https://golfweek.usatoday.com/story/sports/golf/pga/2026/02/11/2026-att-pebble-beach-pro-am-chris-gotterup-pebble-beach-childhood-bet-dad/88629258007/ |title=From childhood bet to world No. 5, Chris Gotterup loves Pebble Beach |magazine=Golfweek |first=Adam |last=Schupak |date=February 11, 2026}} In July 2026, Gotterup rallied from a five-shot deficit in the final round by closing with a 9-under 62 to win the [[John Deere Classic]].{{cite news |title=Chris Gotterup wins John Deere Classic with a 62 and late help from Ben Kohles |url=https://apnews.com/article/chris-gotterup-john-deere-classic-ben-kohles-84e510f6fe5659dea04e34b7cd93872e |work=Associated Press News |access-date=6 July 2026 |date=5 July 2026}} In September 2026, Gotterup made his Presidents Cup debut as a member of the United States team and won his singles match against [[Christiaan Bezuidenhout]].{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/golf/player/scorecards/_/id/4690755/chris-gotterup |title=Presidents Cup – Chris Gotterup |work=ESPN}} ==Amateur wins== *2019 [[Metropolitan Amateur]], Fighting Irish Classic '''Robyn Niayuq Frier''' (formerly '''Burke'''; born 1991) is an American politician and member of the [[Alaska House of Representatives]] from the 40th district, which includes the [[North Slope Borough, Alaska|North Slope Borough]] and [[Northwest Arctic Borough, Alaska|Northwest Arctic Borough]]. A [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]], she defeated incumbent [[Thomas Baker (Alaska politician)|Thomas Baker]] in [[2024 Alaska House of Representatives election|2024]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brooks |first=James |date=2024-08-21 |title=Progressive candidates show unusual strength in Alaska state legislative primaries |url=https://alaskapublic.org/2024/08/21/progressive-candidates-show-unusual-strength-in-alaska-state-legislative-primaries/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Alaska Public Media |language=en-US}}</ref> The district is the size of [[Germany]], and is the northernmost legislative district in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruskin |first=Liz |date=2024-08-05 |title=How to run in a House district the size of Germany? Pickled whale might help. |url=https://alaskapublic.org/2024/08/05/how-to-run-in-a-house-district-the-size-of-germany-pickled-whale-might-help/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Alaska Public Media |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Brooks |first=James |title=America's farthest-north state House race is now tied, as more votes are counted in Alaska primary|newspaper=Alaska Beacon|publisher=[[States Newsroom]] |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/briefs/americas-farthest-north-state-house-race-is-now-tied-as-more-votes-are-counted-in-alaska-primary/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |language=en-US}}</ref> She was previously the president of the [[North Slope Borough School District]] Board of Education.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naiden |first=Alena |date=April 24, 2024 |title=Two candidates enter race for House District 40 seat highlighting education needs and public safety |url=https://cdn-www.adn.arcpublishing.com/arctic-sounder/news/2024/04/24/two-candidates-enter-race-for-house-district-40-seat-highlighting-education-needs-and-public-safety/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Anchorage Daily News |language=en}}</ref> In the campaign, issues included water use and wealth inequality.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosen |first=Yereth |date=August 21, 2024 |title=Arctic Alaska House race focuses on issues that candidates say unite the remote region |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/alaska-legislature/2024/09/22/arctic-alaska-house-race-focuses-on-issues-that-candidates-say-unite-the-remote-region/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Anchorage Daily News |language=en}}</ref>

Frier is [[Alaska Natives|Alaska Native]] of [[Iñupiat|Iñupiaq]] descent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Burke wins race to represent Alaska's House District 40 |url=https://www.adn.com/arctic-sounder/news/2024/11/21/burke-wins-in-a-race-to-represent-alaskas-house-district-40/ |first=Alena|last=Naiden|date=November 21, 2024 |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[Anchorage Daily News|The Arctic Sounder]]}}</ref>

'''Chloé Dufresne''' (born 1991, [[Montpellier]]) is a French conductor. 

==Biography==
Raised in the Montpellier neighbourhood of La Chamberte,<ref>{{cite news | author=Virginie Vives | title=Chloé Dufresne, cheffe d'orchestre montpelliéraine | url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/francebleu/podcasts/l-invite-qui-prend-son-temps/chloe-dufresne-cheffe-d-orchestre-montpellieraine-8927890 | work=France Musique | date=2023-10-01 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref> Dufresne studied singing and piano as a youth, and began viola studies at age eight.  She also sang in the children's choir of the [[Opéra national de Montpellier]].<ref name="CJM2022">{{cite news | author=Côme Jocteur-Monrozier | title=Chloé Dufresne, révélation des Victoires de la musique classique 2022 | url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/chloe-dufresne-revelation-des-victoires-de-la-musique-classique-2022-8505955 | work=France Musique | date=2022-01-31 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>  She continued her music studies at the [[Sibelius Academy]], where her teachers included [[Sakari Oramo]].  Dufresne earned a bachelor's degree and subsequently a master's degree from the Sibelius Academy.  For a year, she continued her conducting studies with [[Alain Altinoglu]] at the [[Conservatoire de Paris]].

In 2020, Dufresne was a finalist in the Siemens-Hallé Competition in Manchester.  In 2021, she won third prize at the [[Malko Competition]],<ref name="Mulson">{{cite news | author=Jennifer Mulson | title=Colorado Springs Philharmonic announces new music director | url=https://gazette.com/arts-entertainment/colorado-springs-philharmonic-announces-new-music-director/article_d4d1ed10-85e9-4628-bd87-9ddc57504f0f.html | work=The Denver Gazette | date=2025-07-29 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref> and two ''coups de cœur'' prizes (audience and orchestral) and as well as a "special mention" at the [[International Besançon Competition for Young Conductors]].

Dufresne was one of the three finalist nominees for the 2022 ''Victoires de la Musique Classique'' Awards.<ref name="CJM2022"/><ref>{{cite news | author= | title=Cérémonie des 29e Victoires de la Musique Classique du mercredi 09 mars 2022 | url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/soiree-speciale-des-victoires-de-la-musique-classique/ceremonie-des-29emes-victoires-de-la-musique-classique-du-mercredi-09-mars-2022-7451502 | work=France Musique | date=2022-03-09 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>  She was an assistant conductor and [[Gustavo Dudamel|Dudamel]] Fellow with the [[Los Angeles Philharmonic]] for the 2022–2023 season.<ref>{{cite news | author= | title=Chloé Dufresne, brillante jeune cheffe de Montpellier à Los Angeles | url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/l-invite-du-jour/chloe-dufresne-brillante-jeune-cheffe-de-montpellier-a-los-angeles-7037609 | work=France Musique | date=2022-09-05 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>  In June 2022, the Orchestre Ostinato announced the appointment of a collective of five musicians, including Dufresne, to oversee the ensemble's artistic direction.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://ostinato.fr/index.php/2022/06/30/une-nouvelle-direction-artistique/ | title=Une nouvelle direction artistique | publisher=Orchestre Ostinato | date=30 June 2022 | access-date=2025-09-16}}</ref>

In January 2024, Dufresne first guest-conducted the [[Colorado Springs Philharmonic]].<ref name="Jones2025">{{cite news | author=Jeremy Jones | title=Philharmonic Names Chloé Dufresne as New Music Director | url=https://springsmag.com/philharmonic-names-chloe-dufresne-as-new-music-director/ | work=Springs Magazine | date=2025-07-29 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>  In July 2025, the orchestra announced the appointment of Dufresne as its next music director, effective with the 2025–2026 season, with an initial contract of three seasons.<ref name="Mulson"/><ref>{{cite press release | url=https://csphilharmonic.org/2025/08/downbeatofnewera/ | title=The Downbeat of a New Era | publisher=Colorado Springs Philharmonic | date=14 August 2025 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author=Rebecca Gvozden | title='We had 250 applications from all over the world': Colorado Springs Philharmonic names new music director | url=https://www.kktv.com/2025/07/30/we-had-250-applications-all-over-world-colorado-springs-philharmonic-has-new-music-director/ | work=KKTV | date=2025-07-30 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>  This appointment marks her first music directorship.  Dufresne is the first female conductor to be named music director of the Colorado Springs Philharmonic.<ref name="Jones2025"/>

Dufresne and her family live in Paris.<ref>{{cite news | author=Chelsea Casabona | title=Colorado Springs Philharmonic announces Chloé Dufresne as its next maestro | url=https://www.rmpbs.org/blogs/arts-culture/colorado-springs-philharmonic-chloe-dufresne | work=Rocky Mountain PBS | date=2025-08-07 | access-date=2025-09-12}}</ref>

'''{{nihongo|Yusaku Ito|伊東優作|Itō Yūsaku}}''' is a Japanese [[professional wrestler]] signed to Dove Pro Wrestling, best known for his tenure with [[Big Japan Pro Wrestling]] (BJW) and [[Pro Wrestling Freedoms]]. He also makes appearances in various promotions from the Japanese independent scene.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.profightdb.com/wrestlers/yusaku-ito-21240.html|title=Yusaku Ito Profile & Match Listing|work=profightdb.com|author=Internet Wrestling Database (IWD)|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref>

==Professional wrestling career==
===Japanese independent circuit (2011–present)===
Ito made his [[professional wrestling]] debut at a [[house show]] promoted by Daiwa Entertainment Pro Wrestling on September 18, 2011, where he fell short to Michio Kageyama in singles competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=259875|title=DEP Dojo Show|work=cagematch.de|first=Philip|last=Kreikenbohm|date=September 18, 2011|access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> He worked for various [[hardcore wrestling]] promotions of the Japanese independent circuit such as Deathmatch Innovative Element (DIE), [[Pro Wrestling Freedoms]], Pro Wrestling Heat Up, Daiwa Entertainment Pro Wrestling (DEP) and others.<ref name="Data"/>

At ''GCW/JCW Vs. The World 2024'', an event promoted by [[Game Changer Wrestling]] on April 4, 2024, Ito competed in a [[tag team match|fourteen-man tag team match]] in which he teamed up with [[Ho Ho Lun]], [[LJ Cleary]], Lou Nixon, [[Mizuki Watase]], [[Ricky Knight Jr.]] and [[Shota (wrestler)|Shota]] in a losing effort against [[Calvin Tankman]], Charlie Tiger, Marcus Mathers, [[Mike Bailey (wrestler)|Mike Bailey]], Mr. Danger, Terry Yaki and [[Tony Deppen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://prowrestling.net/site/2024/04/05/gcw-jcw-vs-the-world-results-4-4-vetters-review-of-gringo-loco-arez-and-latigo-vs-yamato-dragon-kid-and-shun-skywalker-masha-slamovich-vs-syuri-for-the-jcw-title-aigle-blanc-vs-jordan-o/|title=GCW/JCW vs. The World results (4/4): Vetter's review of Gringo Loco, Arez, and Latigo vs. Yamato, Dragon Kid, and Shun Skywalker, Masha Slamovich vs. Syuri for the JCW Title, Aigle Blanc vs. Jordan Oliver|work=[[Pro Wrestling Dot Net]]|first=Chris|last=Vetter|date=April 5, 2024|access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref>

===Pro Wrestling Freedoms (2012–present)===
Ito made his debut in [[Pro Wrestling Freedoms]] at ''FREEDOMS Toru Sugiura Hometown Comeback 2012'' on October 21, where he teamed up with Kengo Takai in a losing effort against [[Takayasu Fukuda|Bear Fukuda]] and [[Keizo Matsuda]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=89593|title=FREEDOMS Toru Sugiura Hometown Comeback 2012|work=cagematch.de|first=Philip|last=Kreikenbohm|date=October 21, 2012|access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> During his time with the promotion, he chased for various titles. He won the [[King of Freedom World Tag Team Championship]] by teaming up with [[Masashi Takeda]] at ''Freedoms The Gekokujo 2025'' on March 19, where they defeated Kenji Fukimoto and [[Violento Jack]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pw-freedoms.co.jp/event_detail.php?id=3063|script-title=ja:2025.3.19　東京・後楽園ホール 2025年03月19日　開始時刻：18時30分|work=[[Pro Wrestling Freedoms]]|language=ja|date=March 19, 2025|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> At ''Jun Kasai Produce Tokyo Death Match Carnival 2025 Vol. 1'' on July 10, Ito unsuccessfully challenged [[Toru Sugiura]] for the [[King of Freedom World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bodyslam.net/2025/07/10/freedoms-tokyo-death-match-carnival-vol-1-results-july-10th-2025/|title=Freedoms Tokyo Death Match Carnival Vol 1 Results (July 10th, 2025)|work=bodyslam.net|first=Ethan|last=Black|date=July 16, 2025|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref>

===Big Japan Pro Wrestling (2021–present)===
Ito made his debut in [[Big Japan Pro Wrestling]] at ''BJW Death Market 61'' on May 30, 2021, where he teamed up with Makoto Hasuka to defeat [[Akira Hyodo]] and [[Kosuke Sato (wrestler)|Kosuke Sato]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=323079|title=BJW Death Market 61|work=cagematch.net|first=Philip|last=Kreikenbohm|date=May 30, 2021|access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> During his tenure with the promotion, he chased for various accomplishments. At ''BJW Death Mania X 2022'' on August 28, he teamed up with Michio Kageyama and unsuccessfully challenged Astronauts ([[Fuminori Abe]] and [[Takuya Nomura (wrestler)|Takuya Nomura]]) for the [[BJW Tag Team Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/bjw-death-mania-x-2022-hay-nuevo-monarca-death-match/|title=BJW: «Death Mania X 2022» Hay nuevo monarca Death Match|work=[[Superluchas.com]]|author=Dark Angelita|language=Spanish|date=September 2, 2022|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref> At ''BJW Death Mania XI 2023'' on September 10, Ito unsuccessfully challenged [[Yuki Ishikawa (wrestler, born 1995)|Yuki Ishikawa]] for the [[BJW Deathmatch Heavyweight Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pwmania.com/bjw-death-mania-11-results-september-10-2023|title=BJW Death Mania 11 Results – September 10, 2023|work=pwmania.com|first=Ethan|last=Black|date=September 10, 2023|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref> He eventually succeeded in winning the title at ''BJW Death Mania XIII 2025'' on August 24, by defeating [[Akira (American wrestler)|Akira]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bodyslam.net/2025/08/24/bjw-death-mania-13-results-august-24th-2025/|title=BJW Death Mania 13 Results (August 24th, 2025)|work=bodyslam.net|first=Ethan|last=Black|date=August 30, 2025|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref>

Ito competed in various of the promotion's signature events. In the [[Saikyo Tag League]], he made his first appaearance at the 2022 edition where he teamed up with Michio Kageyama, placing themselves in the B block of the competition and scoring a total of eight points after going against the teams of [[Masashi Takeda]] and [[Takumi Tsukamoto]], [[Abdullah Kobayashi]] and [[Daiju Wakamatsu]], [[Shigehiro Irie]] and [[Yuya Aoki (wrestler)|Yuya Aoki]], [[Daichi Hashimoto]] and [[Hideyoshi Kamitani]], Chicharito Shoki and [[Yuji Okabayashi]], [[Kazuki Hashimoto]] and Satsuki Nagao, [[Kankuro Hoshino]] and Yuichi Taniguchi, and [[Brahman Brothers|Brahman Kei and Brahman Shu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/bjw-saikyou-tag-league-2022-gran-final/|title=BJW:«Saikyou Tag League 2022» Gran Final|work=[[Superluchas.com]]|author=Dark Angelita|language=Spanish|date=February 24, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2023}}</ref>

'''Sebastian Declan Murphy''' (born March 6, 1990) is a [[Swedish Americans|Swedish-American]] singer, former [[tattoo artist]] and [[Lead vocalist|front man]] and only foreign-born member of the [[Stockholm]]-based [[Post-punk|post-punk]] band [[Viagra Boys]] since 2015 and the jazz band Grismask since 2021.

== Pre-band life ==
Sebastian Murphy was born in [[San Rafael, California]] to an American father, who worked as a [[Bank|banker]], and a Swedish mother. Murphy became a drug addict which led to him being arrested when he was 15. In 2007, when he was 17 years old, he dropped out of high school and traveled to [[Stockholm]] where he lived with his aunt for several years. He became employed as a [[tattoo artist]] and became a member of the band, Viagra Boys, after they saw Murphy drunkenly perform [[Mariah Carey]]'s song "[[We Belong Together]]" at a [[karaoke]] night.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-29 |title=Murphy: Var omöjligt att uppträda nykter |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/v5LPQl |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=www.aftonbladet.se |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-06 |title=Sebastian Murphy från Viagra Boys: ”Jag har alltid skrivit låtar från ett ställe av extrem ångest” |url=https://www.dn.se/kultur/sebastian-murphy-fran-viagra-boys-jag-har-alltid-skrivit-latar-fran-ett-stalle-av-extrem-angest/ |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=DN.se |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jack |first=Malcolm |date=2025-04-21 |title=Swedish punks Viagra Boys: ‘It’s freeing for people to see a dude let his gut hang out’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2025/apr/21/swedish-punks-viagra-boys-interview-sebastian-murphy-viagr-aboys |access-date=2025-11-30 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

== Music career ==
In 2018, the band released their debut album, ''[[Street Worms]]'', on the Swedish independent label [[Year0001]]. Nils Hansson of ''[[Dagens Nyheter]]'' described the band favorably, praising their musical style as well as their use of black humor and satire, and rated the album 5/5. In 2019, the band won the [[Independent Music Companies Association]] (IMPALA) Album of the Year Award for ''Street Worms''.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-09-28 |title=Dagens skiva: Viagra Boys är mycket mer än bara enkelspåriga |url=https://www.dn.se/kultur-noje/skivrecensioner/dagens-skiva-viagra-boys-ar-mycket-mer-an-bara-enkelspariga/ |access-date=2025-11-30 |work=Dagens Nyheter |language=sv |issn=1101-2447}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=VIAGRA BOYS - Album of the Year WINNER 2019 {{!}} Impala |url=https://impalamusic.org/content/viagra-boys-album-year-winner-2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929051527/https://impalamusic.org/content/viagra-boys-album-year-winner-2019 |archive-date=2020-09-29 |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=impalamusic.org |language=en}}</ref>

The band's second album, ''[[Welfare Jazz]]'', was released in January 2021. In October of that same year, founding member and guitarist Benjamin Vallé died at the age of 47. While he appeared on ''Welfare Jazz'', he was not an active member of the band at the time of his death. A deluxe edition of ''Welfare Jazz'' released in 2022, featuring new [[Album cover|album art]] and seven new tracks.
[[File:Viagra Boys - 44414604600.jpg|thumb|Sebastian Murphy in [[Malmö|Malmö, Sweden]]]]
Viagra Boys' third studio album, ''[[Cave World]]'', was released in July 2022. The band played at multiple festivals in 2022, including [[Coachella (festival)|Coachella]] and [[Primavera Sound]], and performed at [[Glastonbury Festival|Glastonbury]] in 2023. While touring in support of ''Cave World'', they recorded a concert film during their February 23, 2023 show at [[The Salt Shed]], which was later streamed and released for free on YouTube. Viagra Boys won the Swedish [[Grammis]] award for Rock of the Year in 2023, and supported [[Queens of the Stone Age]] during their North American tour that same year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-06 |title=Queens Of The Stone Age Announce North American Tour With Phantogram, Viagra Boys, The Armed, & Jehnny Beth |url=https://stereogum.com/2226162/queens-of-the-stone-age-announce-north-american-tour-with-phantogram-viagra-boys-the-armed-jehnny-beth/news/ |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=stereogum.com |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2025, Viagra Boys announced ''[[Viagr Aboys]]'', which was released on 25 April via their newly launched label ''Shrimptech Enterprise''s. That year they also embarked on "''the infinite anxiety tour''" in support of the album, playing shows across Europe, North America, Oceania, and Japan. The tour is set to include the band's biggest shows to-date, including performances at [[Alexandra Palace]] in [[London]] and [[Avicii Arena]] in Stockholm.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Viagra Boys Announce New Album viagr aboys |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/viagra-boys/viagra-boys-announce-new-album-viagr-aboys |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=Paste Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-06 |title=Punk’s Not Dead: It's Now Just a Bunch of Shrimp-Obsessed Swedish Guys |url=https://www.maristcircle.com/arts-entertainment/2025/5/6/punks-not-dead-its-now-just-a-bunch-of-shrimp-obsessed-swedish-guys |access-date=2025-11-30 |website=MARIST CIRCLE |language=en-US}}</ref>
[[File:QOTSARnRCircShef270825-20 (54784392103).jpg|thumb|Sebastian Murphy in England (2025)]]

== Personal life ==
Sebastian speaks both [[English language|English]] and [[Swedish language|Swedish]] fluently.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZSdb1aWInOc |title=Sebastian Murphy (Viagra boys) - Interview @ Bianca by night 2025 |date=2025-02-10 |last=HojasLive |access-date=2025-11-30 |via=YouTube}}</ref> He currently lives with and is in a romantic relationship with [[Moa Romanova]], a Swedish cartoonist from [[Kramfors]]. Murphy has several tattoos across his body including the word "Lös" (the Swedish word for "Loose") across his forehead.

'''Angelo Iannelli''' (born 17 July 1986 in [[Benevento]], Italy)<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/eol-iannelli-angelo|title=Iannelli, Angelo|encyclopedia=[[Treccani|Treccani Encyclopedia]]}}</ref> is an Italian singer-songwriter, writer, actor, playwright and filmmaker, known for blending auteur songwriting styles, folk-rock and indie-pop. His genre mixes singer-songwriter introspection with indie pop narrative and folk-rock structures, creating an original literary-minded musical style.

==Early life==
Angelo Iannelli was born in [[Benevento]], but due to his father's work, he spent his childhood and adolescence between Florence, Brindisi, Frosinone, Malta, and Rome, where he moved permanently in 2003 and began to frequent the Roman artistic scene, first in the world of acting, where he took part in his first theatrical performances, then in the literary and musical worlds. During this period, he began to write short stories and compose his first songs, influenced by the singer-songwriters of the 1970s,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ilgiornaleoff.it/2017/12/14/non-e-tardi-per-riprenderci-i-nostri-sogni/|title=Con questo album Angelo Iannelli ci dice che non è tardi per riprenderci i nostri sogni|work=[[Il Giornale]]|author=Angela Lonardo|language=Italian|access-date=4 October 2024|date=14 December 2017}}</ref> particularly [[Rino Gaetano]],<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://euterpemusica.it/2024/03/13/quattro-chiacchiere-col-talento-puro-di-angelo-iannelli-2/|work=Euterpe musica|title= Quattro chiacchiere col talento puro di Angelo Iannelli|language=Italian|access-date=30 July 2024|date=13 March 2024}}</ref> [[Antonello Venditti]], [[Edoardo Bennato]], [[Cat Stevens]] and, above all, [[Francesco De Gregori]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://indieitaliamag.it/2021/10/19/angelo-iannelli-il-mio-fortuito-incontro-con-malbene-intervista-indie-italia-mag/|work=Indie Italia Mag|title=Angelo Iannelli: "Il mio fortuito incontro con Malbene"|author= Vincent Hank|language=Italian|access-date=30 July 2024|date=19 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://paroleindie.it/angelo-iannelli-presenta-malbene-il-suo-nuovo-singolo|work=Parole Indie|title=Angelo Iannelli presenta "Malbene" – il suo nuovo singolo|language=Italian|date=22 October 2021|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref>
After graduating from the [[Eugenio Montale]] classical high school in Rome in 2005, he enrolled in the DAMS degree course at the Faculty of Letters and Philosophy at the University of Roma Tre, where he graduated with a thesis in acting pedagogy,<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.mondospettacolo.com/angelo-iannelli-sempre-a-due-passi-dai-margini/|work=Mondo spettacolo|title= Angelo Iannelli: sempre a due passi dai margini|date=3 September 2024 |language=Italian|access-date=4 October 2024}}</ref> and subsequently continued his studies on cinema by enrolling in a master's degree course at the same faculty, where he developed a passion for the philosophy of art, the psychology of art and applied psychoanalysis, and graduated with a thesis in Aesthetics Philosophy.

During his university years, he studied acting with Carlo Merlo, a former professor at the [[Accademia Nazionale di Arte Drammatica Silvio D'Amico]] in Rome, and began teaching directing, playwriting, and screenwriting at the Clesis Arte school in Rome, directed by Merlo himself. During the same period, he wrote articles on literature, art, and culture for ''L'Eco del litorale'' and ''Roma Capitale Magazine'', which were later republished by the magazine "PirandelloWeb",<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pirandelloweb.com/pirandello-un-regista-e-uno-sceneggiatore-mancato/|title=Pirandello, un regista (e uno sceneggiatore) mancato|author=Angelo Iannelli|work=PirandelloWeb|language=italian|date=25 October 2022|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref> and wrote the screenplays for and directed several independent short films.
He later specialized in literature and, once he obtained his teaching qualification, became a high school literature teacher.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://roma.repubblica.it/cronaca/2016/07/26/news/anzio_domenica_31_il_concerto_di_angelo_iannelli-144836551/|title=Anzio, domenica 31 luglio il concerto di Angelo Iannelli|work=[[La Repubblica]]|language=italian|date=26 July 2016|access-date=30 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.2duerighe.com/musica/96157-angelo-iannelli-intervista-musica-scuola.html|work=2duerighe|title=Intervista ad Angelo Iannelli: "La musica è il motore delle mie giornate"|author=Rosella Maiorana|language=Italian|date=28 December 2017|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.standout-zine.it/intervista-a-angelo-iannelli/|work=Standout Webzine|title=Intervista al cantautore romano Angelo Iannelli|language=Italian|date=15 December 2017|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref>

==Literary career==
After several theoretical-critical writings on philosophy, literature, music, acting pedagogy, and the interrelationships between art and psychoanalysis, in 2012 he wrote the text for the theatrical performance ''Dalla notte del mito all'Eneide, nei luoghi e nei tempi di Virgilio'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://napoli.repubblica.it/cronaca/2012/04/29/news/palinuro_michele_placido_legge_l_eneide-34171309/|title=Palinuro, Michele Placido legge l'Eneide|work=[[La Repubblica]]|language=Italian|date=29 April 2012|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://spettacolo.iltabloid.it/2017/11/30/conserva-i-sogni-singolo-angelo-iannelli.html|title= Conserva i sogni il nuovo singolo di Angelo Iannelli|work=Il Tabloid Spettacolo| language=Italian|date=30 November 2017|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref> which he performed with [[Michele Placido]] and [[Alessandro Haber]].
The following year he published the scientific essay ''[[L'Io diviso. Dai medici-filosofi alla letteratura, al teatro e al cinema del Novecento]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://goodmorningromanews.wordpress.com/2013/11/19/lio-diviso-dai-medici-filosofi-alla-letteratura-al-teatro-e-al-cinema-del-novecento|title= L'Io diviso. Dai medici-filosofi alla letteratura, al teatro e al cinema del Novecento. |author=Livia de Pietro|date=19 November 2013|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref> which is included in the catalogues of international universities and libraries and is a bibliographical source on [[Luigi Pirandello]], on the theme of the double, and on the contribution of experimental psychology to twentieth-century culture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.italianisti.it/pubblicazioni/atti-di-congresso/letteratura-e-scienze/02%20COSENTINO.pdf|title=Finzione letteraria, inconscio e malattia ne L'illusione di Federico De Roberto|author=Paola Cosentino|date=14 September 2019|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.persee.fr/authority/49484|title= Binet, Alfred }}</ref>
In 2016, the novel ''[[Bar Binario]]'' was published, a coming-of-age story set in an imaginary nocturnal Rome.
In 2023, his third book was published, the essay ''[[Il Metodo V.D.A.M. di Carlo Merlo. Una pedagogia attorica]]'', based on the documentary he authored, ''Intervista a Carlo Merlo, il maestro delle Star'' – which explores and compares the most important contemporary acting methods, including the [[Stanislavski's system]].

==Career as actor, screenwriter, and director==
After studying acting and some theatrical experience, including the role of Creon in [[Euripides]]' [[Medea]] directed by Emanuele Faina and performed in various Roman theaters, since 2009 he has written, directed, and acted in several independent short films,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://italiancinemaarttoday.blogspot.com/2012/12/new-faces-of-italian-cinema-with-2012.html|title=New faces of Italian cinema|date=11 December 2012|author=Jeannine Guilyard|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref> the best known of which is ''Il nulla alle spalle''.

Since 2011, he has begun acting in various TV series,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rockit.it/angeloiannelli/biografia|title= Angelo Iannelli|work=Rockit|language=Italian}}</ref> including ''[[Squadra antimafia - Palermo oggi]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.filmbooster.com.au/creator/828679-angelo-iannelli/biography/|title=Angelo Iannelli|work=Filmbooster|language=Italian}}</ref> ''[[R.I.S. Roma – Delitti imperfetti]]'', ''[[Il peccato e la vergogna]]'', ''[[L'onore e il rispetto]]'', ''[[Un medico in famiglia]]'', up to the most recent, ''[[Che Dio ci aiuti]]'' (2023), ''Il clandestino''<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.filmaffinity.com/us/fullcredits.php?movie_id=610755|title= Il clandestino|work= filmaffinity.com}}</ref> (2024) and ''[[Miss Fallaci]]'' (2025), and directed the music videos of his songs "Non lo so" and "DAG".

==Musical career==

==Musical style==
Gifted with a warm and expressive voice, from a musical point of view he has embraced various sounds, from [[pop rock]] to [[indie pop]], passing through [[Folk music|folk]] and rock. In his lyrics<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.mescalina.it/musica/news/7077/musicnewsrelease|title="Paolo a Francesca" del cantautore romano Angelo Iannelli viene recensito da un famoso critico musicale e culturale, docente universitario e poeta (Lorenzo Fiorito)|language=Italian|access-date=4 October 2024}}</ref> there is an extensive use of metaphors, oxymorons and synesthesia, which often give rise to two parallel narrative levels, one simple and direct and the other not immediately interpretable; with an often poetic,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/eol-iannelli-angelo/|work=[[Treccani]]|language=Italian|access-date=4 October 2024|title= Iannelli, Angelo }}</ref> melancholic<ref>{{cite magazine|title = Angelo Iannelli – Vicini margini | author = Gianluca Clerici |magazine = Raropiù n° 124|language=Italian|date = July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://paroleindie.it/angelo-iannelli-dag-il-suo-nuovo-brano|title=Angelo Iannelli: "DAG" il suo nuovo brano|author=Greta Anello|language=Italian|date=20 October 2020|access-date=26 March 2025}}</ref> romantic and intimate approach, as well as ironic on several occasions, he has treated interior and social themes with an original style, such as existential unease and the search for identity in contemporary society.
