'''Sally Fuesaina''' (born 15 February 1992) is an [[Australians|Australian]] [[rugby union]] player. She represents {{nwrut|Australia}} internationally and plays for the [[ACT Brumbies Women|ACT Brumbies]] in the [[Super Rugby Women's]] competition.

==Early life==
Fuesaina played [[rugby league]] and [[rugby union]] as a child, but stopped at the age of twelve and only started playing rugby union again in her late teens.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-18 |title=How I Got Here: Faasasalu Fuesaina |url=https://brumbies.rugby/news/how-i-got-here-faasasalu-fuesaina-2024418 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=brumbies.rugby |language=en}}</ref>

== Rugby career ==
Fuesaina joined the Western Sydney Two Blues women’s team in 2022, she then made her [[Super Rugby Women's]] debut for the [[ACT Brumbies Women|ACT Brumbies]] against the [[Fijian Drua Women|Fijian Drua]] in 2023.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Payten |first=Iain |date=2024-05-10 |title=She dusted off her boots to beat depression. Now this scrum mum is about to play for Australia |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/rugby-union/she-dusted-off-her-boots-to-beat-depression-now-this-scrum-mum-is-about-to-play-for-australia-20240510-p5jchl.html |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}}</ref>

She made her international debut for {{nwrut|Australia}} against {{nwrut|Canada}} in the [[2024 Pacific Four Series]], she came off the bench in the 72nd <abbr>minute</abbr> of the match.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Nathan |date=2024-10-11 |title=From Samoa to South Africa: Wallaroos prop Sally Fuesaina eager to tighten knowledge of scrummaging dark arts |url=https://www.rugby.com.au/news/wallaroos-prop-sally-fuesaina-eager-to-tighten-her-knowledge-the-scrummaging-dark-arts-20241010 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.rugby.com.au |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Nathan |date=2024-09-01 |title=Wallaroos squad confirmed for European Tour, WXV 2 |url=https://www.rugby.com.au/news/wallaroos-squad-confirmed-for-european-tour-wxv-2-202491 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.rugby.com.au |language=en}}</ref> She also featured in the games against the [[New Zealand women's national rugby union team|Black Ferns]] and the {{nwrut|United States}}.<ref name=":2" /> In July 2024, she was set to play for [[Australia A women's national rugby union team|Australia A]] against {{nwrut|Samoa}} in [[Apia]] after missing out on selection for the [[Australia women's national rugby union team|Wallaroos]], but was called-up for the senior side as an injury replacement for [[Brianna Hoy]].<ref name=":2" /> 

Fuesaina also appeared for the triumphant Wallaroos in their maiden [[2024 WXV#WXV 2|WXV 2]] title win in [[South Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-10 |title=Five Brumbies set for Wallaroos WXV 2 title decider against Scotland |url=https://brumbies.rugby/news/wallaroos-20241010 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=brumbies.rugby |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-12 |title=Match Report: Australia 31-22 Scotland |url=https://scottishrugby.org/news-and-features/match-report-australia-31-22-scotland/ |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=scottishrugby.org}}</ref>

In 2025, she was part of the Wallaroos 46-player contracted squad that was announced for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Nathan |date=2025-02-11 |title=Wallaroos contracted squad announced for 2025 season |url=https://www.rugby.com.au/news/wallaroos-contracted-squad-announced-for-2025-season-2025211 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.rugby.com.au |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Perkins |first=Bruce |date=2025-02-11 |title=New Contracts for Wallaroos |url=http://4theloveofsport.co.uk/2025/02/11/new-contracts-for-wallaroos/ |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=4 The Love Of Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> She represented Australia A against {{nwrut|Samoa}} in [[Canberra]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wasiliev |first=Nick |date=2025-06-26 |title=New look Australia A side set to face Manusina as World Cup challengers push their case |url=https://www.rugby.com.au/news/new-look-australia-a-side-set-to-face-samoa-as-world-cup-challengers-push-their-case-2025625 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.rugby.com.au |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Fuesaina is the mother of two daughters, Athena and Luna.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She suffered [[Postpartum depression|post-partum depression]] after having Luna, her return to [[Rugby union|rugby]] helped her recovery and led to her playing for the ACT Brumbies and Wallaroos.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-16 |title=How Rugby Union saved Sally Fuesaina after postpartum depression |url=https://www.abc.net.au/pacific/programs/nesian-footy/nesian-footy-sally-fuesaina-wallaroos/104331786 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=ABC Pacific |language=en-AU}}</ref>

=== United Brothel Workers ===
In 2026, Jetson became the spokesperson for workers at [[Sheri's Ranch]], a legal [[brothel]] in [[Pahrump, Nevada]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Jessica |title=Sex workers at Nevada brothel fight for the first unionization |url=https://apnews.com/article/nevada-brothel-sex-workers-unionizing-eacf41f41bee5cfe5c13d3dfc4a1887c |website=AP News |publisher=The Associated Press |access-date=18 February 2026}}</ref> Nevada is the only state in the nation where [[Prostitution in Nevada|prostitution is legal]]. Reali: «Voy a dar lo mejor de mí para quedarme» |url=https://pasealaliga.com.ar/m-reali-voy-a-dar-lo-mejor-de-mi-para-quedarme/ |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=Pase a la Liga |language=es}}</ref>. After the trial, he then joined Villa San Carlos' local rivals [[Defensores de Cambaceres]], where he scored 4 goals to become the team's top goalscorer for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-06-26 |title=De la D a la Libertadores: la historia del nuevo refuerzo de San Lorenzo {{Short description|Argentinian artist (born 1989)}}

'''La Chola Poblete''' (born 1989 Mendoza ) is an Argentinian [[Multidisciplinary arts|multidisciplinary artist]] and activist. She is known for sculpture, painting, performance art, drawing, photography, and video art. Her art primarily focuses on femininity, queerness and indigenous roots.<ref name="Ezquiaga-2024">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stirworld.com/see-features-in-venice-latin-american-artists-highlight-historically-silenced-voices|title=In Venice, Latin American artists highlight historically silenced voices|first=Mercedes|last=Ezquiaga|date=July 15, 2024|website=Stir World}}</ref> She resides in [[Buenos Aires]].<ref name="Aguerregaray-2024">{{Cite web |last=Aguerregaray |first=Julieta |date=November 18, 2024 |title=La Chola Poblete: The voice of Mendoza conquering international contemporary art |url=https://www.timeout.com/buenos-aires/la-chola-poblete-the-voice-of-mendoza-conquering-international-contemporary-art|website=Time Out Buenos Aires|type=interview}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
La Chola Poblete was born in 1989 in the city of Guaymallén, in [[Mendoza Department|Mendoza]], Argentina.<ref name="Ezquiaga-2024" /><ref name="Batalla-2024">{{Cite web |last=Batalla |first=Juan |date=February 2, 2024 |title=Quién es “La Chola” Poblete, la artista argentina elegida para la muestra central de la Bienal de Venecia |url=https://www.infobae.com/cultura/2024/02/02/quien-es-la-chola-poblete-la-artista-argentina-elegida-para-la-muestra-central-de-la-bienal-de-venecia/ |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=infobae |language=es}}</ref><ref name="Deutsche Bank-2023" /> She is of Bolivian heritage, and is [[Transgender|trans]].<ref name="Aguerregaray-2024" /><ref name="Lang-2021">{{Cite web |last=Lang |first=Silvio |date=June 11, 2021 |title=Mauricio "La Chola" Poblete presenta su muestra "Tenedor de hereje" |url=https://www.pagina12.com.ar/347314-mauricio-la-chola-poblete-presenta-su-muestra-tenedor-de-her |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=Página{{!}}12 |language=es}}</ref> She was raised in a matriarchal family by a single mom and multiple aunts.<ref name="Aguerregaray-2024" /> Before she took on the identity of La Chola Poblete she spent her formative years as a non-binary indigenous teenager.<ref name="Mendiberry" /> 

She received a bachelors degree and teaching degree in visual arts at the [[National University of Cuyo]] in Mendoza.<ref name="Mendiberry">{{Cite web |title=La Chola Poblete |url=https://metalmagazine.eu/en/post/la-chola-poblete |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=Metal Magazine |language=es|last=Mendiberry|first=Delfina Martinez|type=interview}}</ref>

La Chola Poblete moved in 2017 to Buenos Aires, where she performed as a member of the Comparsa Drag art collective.<ref name="Lang-2021" /> 

== Works and awards ==
=== Deutsche Bank Award (2023) ===
La Chola Poblete won the [[Deutsche Bank]] Artist of the Year award.<ref name="Deutsche Bank-2023">{{Cite web|url=https://www.db.com/news/detail/20230117-argentinian-la-chola-poblete-is-deutsche-bank-s-artist-of-the-year-2023?language_id=1|title=Argentinian La Chola Poblete is Deutsche Bank's “Artist of the Year” 2023|website=Deutsche Bank (DB)|date=January 17, 2023}}</ref> This exhibition Guaymallén, named after her home city, is a tribute to the artist’s indigenous roots and queer identity.<ref name="GoOut-2023">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-08 |title=La Chola Poblete: Guaymallén - 08/09/2023 - 05/02/2024 - PalaisPopulaire - GoOut |url=https://goout.net/en/la-chola-poblete-guaymallen/szfcwow/ |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=goout.net |language=en-GB}}</ref> Through this exhibition, La Chola Poblete addresses the historical roles of women and trans people, in which she explains how femininity is often persecuted and ostracized by ideologies that are patriarchal and religious.<ref name="GoOut-2023" />

=== ''Stranieri Ovunque'' (2024) ===
The [[60th Venice Biennale]] in 2024 she showed her work ''Stranieri Ovunque,'' as part of the exhibition series, ''[[Foreigners Everywhere]].''<ref>{{Cite web |title=La Chola Poblete Was Awarded at the Venice Biennial |url=https://www.artealdia.com/News/LA-CHOLA-POBLETE-WAS-AWARDED-AT-THE-VENICE-BIENNIAL |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=Arte al Día |language=en-US|date=May 3, 2024}}</ref> This is the first time the work of La Chola Poblete was presented her work there. She states “I am the first trans and brown artist from Argentina to reach the Biennale".<ref name="Aguerregaray-2024" /> La Chola Poblete’s watercolors showcase the fluidity that comes from how she identifies and sees her own identity. Within these works La Chola Poblete highlights The Virgin as a multifaceted icon as the centerpiece of her works.<ref name="La Biennale di Venezia-2024">{{Cite web |date=2024-03-11 |title=La Chola Poblete |url=https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2024/nucleo-contemporaneo/la-chola-poblete |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=La Biennale di Venezia |language=en}}</ref> The Virgin embodies the connection  between Western culture and indigenous communities that La Chola Poblete wants to portray.<ref name="La Biennale di Venezia-2024" />

=== ''Ejercicios del Llanto'' (2022) ===
This solo exhibition titled ''Ejercicios del llanto'' [Exercises in Weeping] was presented by Museo De Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires (Museum of Modern Art, Buenos Aires).<ref name="Batalla-2024" /> La Chola Poblete wanted this exhibition to be a tribute to the intimacy of having a diary. She created all the works from this exhibition between 2014 and 2015 when she was having a dilemma regarding her own gender. Within the art works presented she expresses her roots and allusions of sexuality. The form of the diary can be seen as conception of the artist's convictions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=La Chola Poblete: Exercises in Weeping |url=https://museomoderno.org/en/exhibitions/la-chola-poblete-ejercicios-del-llanto/ |access-date=2026-03-21 |website=Museo De Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires |language=en-US|date=2022}}</ref>

'''Bernardo Ramos Ribeiro Ferraz "Buba" Espinho''' (born 24 May 1995) is a Portuguese singer and songwriter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.montepio.org/vantagens-montepio/publicacoes/revista-montepio-digital/edicao-9/no-alentejo-nascemos-com-um-dom-especial/|title=“No Alentejo nascemos com um dom especial”|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Associação Mutualista Montepio|language=pt}}</ref> Alongside [[António Zambujo]] and [[Luís Trigacheiro]], he is one of the most highly regarded singers from [[Alentejo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dili.embaixadaportugal.mne.gov.pt/pt/a-embaixada/noticias/semana-da-lingua-portuguesa-cante-alentejano-com-bernardo-espinho-e-antonio-caixeiro|title=Embaixada de Portugal em Timor-Leste|language=pt}}</ref>

==Early life==
Espinho is the son of the composer of the unusual hit "As Meninas da Ribeira do Sado" - a song by Adiafa -, Luís Espinho, and Maria Rosa Martins Ramos Ribeiro Ferraz Espinho (who passed away in 2023). He comes from a family of artists; the son of a musician and a pianist grandmother, he has been familiar with music since a very young age, especially with [[Cante Alentejano]], a type of traditional music from the [[Baixo Alentejo (intermunicipal community)|Baixo Alentejo]] region, where Espinho comes from.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.montepio.org/vantagens-montepio/publicacoes/revista-montepio-digital/edicao-9/no-alentejo-nascemos-com-um-dom-especial/|title=“No Alentejo nascemos com um dom especial”|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Associação Mutualista Montepio|language=pt}}</ref>

==Career==
Espinho took his first steps in music with Cante Alentejano by joining several groups, such as Os Adiafa, A Moda da Mãe, Os Bubedanas, Mestre Cante and Há Lobos sem Ser Serra. A vast journey that, by 2016, and already assuming his place as a fado singer, led him to win the Grande Noite do Fado at the Coliseu dos Recreios, becoming one of the great promises of the Portuguese musical scene.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jf-santamariamaior.pt/bubaespinho/|title=Buba Espinho|date=2023-10-02|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Junta de Freguesia de Santa Maria Maior|language=pt-PT}}</ref>

After winning the Grande Noite do Fado, Espinho decided to start his solo career. Since then, he has been a regular guest in shows by big names in Portuguese music: [[Rui Veloso]], [[António Zambujo]], [[Ana Moura]], [[Celina da Piedade]], [[Júlio Resende]], among many others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cae.pt/index.php/programacao/musica/1990-buba-espinho|title=BUBA ESPINHO|access-date=2024-07-23|website=cae.pt}}</ref>

From Beja, Espinho went to Lisbon, passing through the city's most iconic Fado Houses, from Faia to Casa de Linhares, from Clube do Fado to Adega Machado, and from there to the main national stages, with memorable performances at the NOS Alive Festival, the Coliseu de Lisboa, Coliseu do Porto, Casa da Música, Centro Cultural de Belém, Ovibeja, and many more. Besides Portugal, Buba is pursuing a career that is expected to be international, performing in countries such as England, Timor-Leste, Spain, Canada, Switzerland, and France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.playpremiosdamusicaportuguesa.pt/nomeados2021/buba-espinho/|title=Buba Espinho – Play – Prémios da Música Portuguesa|access-date=2024-07-23|language=pt-PT}}</ref>

In 2020, Espinho released his first studio album. The album includes "Roubei-te Um Beijo", which features Zambujo on the single and in the video. In addition to this song, the album features [[Raquel Tavares]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Buba Espinho|url=https://open.spotify.com/intl-pt/album/4kTMqr69NIsD3jBum2kRks|date=2020-03-20|accessdate=2024-07-23|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2023, the band [[D.A.M.A]] released the hit song "Casa", featuring Buba Espinho, in homage to Cante Alentejano.<ref>{{cite web|last=Arena|first=Rádio|url=https://radioarena.pt/d-a-m-a-casa-ft-buba-espinho/|title=D.A.M.A - Casa (ft Buba Espinho)|date=2022-11-25|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Rádio Arena|language=pt-PT}}</ref> In the same year, Espinho released the song "Ao Teu Ouvido", with [[Bárbara Tinoco]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vozdaplanicie.pt/musica/buba-espinho-e-barbara-tinoco-cantam-juntos-ao-teu-ouvido|title=Buba Espinho e Bárbara Tinoco cantam juntos “Ao Teu Ouvido”|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Rádio Voz da Planície - 104.5FM - Beja|language=pt}}</ref> The following year, he participated in the [[Festival da Canção 2024]], with the song "Farol", finishing in sixth place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://media.rtp.pt/festivaldacancao/cancoes/o-farol-buba-espinho-lyric-video/|title="O Farol" - Buba Espinho (Lyric Video)|access-date=2024-07-23|website=Festival da Canção|language=pt-PT}}</ref><ref name="Voting">{{cite web |title=Festival da Canção 2024 – Votações |trans-title=Festival da Canção 2024 – Voting |url=https://cdn-images.rtp.pt/mcm/pdf/553/5538e22e236e98d7abceea8797ec6fba1.pdf |publisher=RTP |date=12 March 2024 |access-date=12 March 2024 |language=pt-PT}}</ref>

==Personal life==
As a result of his relationship with Ana Carocinho, Esphino had a daughter, Maria Amália, born on 7 September 2023. The name chosen by the couple for their daughter was in honor of his paternal grandmother.<ref>{{cite web|last=SIC|url=https://sic.pt/programas/casafeliz/no-espaco-de-uma-semana-sao-dois-bebes-buba-espinho-ja-e-pai-e-lanca-o-seu-novo-album-voltar/|title="No espaço de uma semana são dois bebés" - Buba Espinho já é pai e lança o seu novo álbum "Voltar"|date=2023-09-15|access-date=2024-07-24|website=SIC|language=pt-PT}}</ref> After ten years of dating, Espinho and Carocinho separated in 2024.<ref>{{cite web|last=Simões|first=Tiago|url=https://www.novagente.pt/buba-espinho-separado-relacionamento-chega-ao-fim-apos-10-anos|title=Buba Espinho - Separado! Relacionamento chega ao fim após 10 anos|access-date=2024-08-20|website=Revista Nova Gente|language=pt-pt}}</ref>

'''Bria Samone Henderson''' is an American actress. She is best known for playing Dr Jordan Allen in the medical drama series ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]'' and Margaret Sloan in the political drama series ''[[Mrs. America (miniseries)|Mrs. America]]''.

==Early life==
Henderson was born in [[Richmond, Virginia]] on December 31st, 1992.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bria Samone Henderson|url=https://www.amazon.com/prime-video/actor/Bria-Samoné-Henderson/amzn1.dv.gti.50eb8b56-8f05-499e-8dc1-6b5b36b1e282/|access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=amazon.com}}</ref> She graduated with a bachelors degree in drama from [[Spelman College]] in 2015. She received her MFA in Acting at the [[University of Washington]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bria Henderson|url=https://drama.washington.edu/people/bria-henderson|access-date=March 27, 2026 |website=drama.washington.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
Henderson moved to [[Los Angeles]] in 2019 to begin her acting career. When she first arrived she found herself sleeping on couches and having many failed auditions. She eventually landed her first big role playing Margaret Sloan in the political drama series ''[[Mrs. America (miniseries)|Mrs. America]]'' starring [[Cate Blanchett]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Quarantined Talent: Bria Samoné Henderson, Focusing, Working|url=https://goldenglobes.com/articles/quarantined-talent-bria-samone-henderson-focusing-working/|access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=goldenglobes.com}}</ref> Her biggest role so far has been playing Dr Jordan Allen in the medical drama series ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]'' starring [[Freddie Highmore]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=‘The Good Doctor’s Bria Samoné Henderson Signs With Gersh
|url=https://deadline.com/2022/09/the-good-doctor-actress-bria-samone-henderson-signs-with-gersh-1235110145/|website=deadline.com|access-date=March 28, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title='The Good Doctor' Star Bria Henderson Opens Up About a Profound Personal Loss|url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/good-doctor-star-bria-henderson-141625298.html|website=yahoo.com|access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> She made her directing debut with the short film ''Virginality'' which she also starred in.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Meet Bria Henderson|url=https://voyagela.com/interview/meet-bria-henderson-of-los-angeles/|access-date=March 28, 2026|website=voyagela.com}}</ref> She also appeared in the short film “Prepared” and won the award for Outstanding Comedic Actress (Short Film) at the 3rd Annual Micheaux Film Festival.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bria Samoné Henderson|url=https://www.detpress.com/abc/bios/bria-samone-henderson/|access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=detpress.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Henderson is very spiritual. She has received critical acclaim for putting in effort to understand the characters she plays. For example when playing Sloan in [[Mrs. America (miniseries)|Mrs. America]] she looked at an interview from the 70s to improve her performance.<ref>{{Cite web|title=How The Good Doctor's Bria Samoné Henderson Is Like Her Character Dr. Allen - Exclusive|url=https://www.thelist.com/711056/how-the-good-doctors-bria-samone-henderson-is-like-her-character-dr-allen-exclusive/|access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=thelist.com}}</ref>

{{Short description|Australian artist and fashion designer (born 1994)}}
'''Michaela Stark''' (born 1994) is an Australian artist, [[corsetier]], model and [[body image|body diversity]] advocate based in London.<ref name="elle">{{cite news |last1=Johnson-Wheeler |first1=Lara |title=Cut To Size: Meet Michaela Stark, The Designer Reimagining Corsetry |url=https://www.elle.com/uk/fashion/a43387585/cut-to-size-interview-michaela-stark/ |work=Elle |date=23 March 2023}}</ref><ref name="perfect">{{cite web |last1=Asiama |first1=Enam |title=Michaela Stark in conversation with Enam Asiama. |url=https://www.theperfectmagazine.com/features/michaela-stark-in-conversation-with-enam-asiama |website=Perfect}}</ref> She is known for her custom-made, body-distorting [[lingerie]] pieces which straddle the border of art and fashion.<ref name="numero">{{Cite news |language=fr |first=Matthieu |last=Jacquet |title=Comment la créatrice Michaela Stark et le photographe Sølve Sundsbø transforment les corps |url=https://numero.com/mode/comment-la-creatrice-michaela-stark-et-le-photographe-solve-sundsbo-transforment-les-corps/ |work=Numéro}}</ref>

Stark plays with the contrast of delicate materials such as silk, [[taffeta]], muslin, tulle, ribbons, pearls, contrasted against tight, asymmetrical corsets which reshape the body, highlighting bulges and curves.<ref name="harpers">{{cite news |first=Patty |last=Huntington |title=Michaela Stark: Couture lingerie designer and body-morphing artist |url=https://harpersbazaar.com.au/michaela-stark-interview/ |work=Harper's Bazaar Australia |date=29 December 2021}}</ref><ref name="paper">{{cite magazine |first=Mario |last=Abad |magazine=Paper |title=Michaela Stark's Lingerie Challenges Theories of the 'Grotesque Body' |url=https://www.papermag.com/michaela-stark |date=7 December 2022}}</ref> Her looks often reflect the discomfort she felt with her body and clothing as an adolescent.<ref name="vogue"/>

== Early life and education ==
Stark was born in [[Brisbane, Australia]], in 1994.<ref name="bima">{{cite web |title=Confronting Femininity |url=https://www.ima.org.au/exhibitions/confronting-femininity/ |website=Brisbane Institute of Modern Art |date=4 October 2025}}</ref> She became interested in fashion as a teenager, but also suffered from [[dysmorphia]].<ref name="vogue">{{Cite magazine |first=Hannah |last=Jackson |title=Michaela Stark is Fashioning a New Kind of Victoria's Secret Angel |url=https://www.vogue.com/article/michaela-stark-victorias-secret-world-tour |magazine=Vogue |date=26 September 2023}}</ref>

She earned a degree in fashion design from [[Queensland University of Technology]] and completed an exchange at a design school in Milan. One of her teachers offered Stark a three-month internship at the Paris showroom of fashion agent Florence Deschamp. Upon her return to Brisbane, she was determined to return to Europe and in 2017 she moved to London and started an internship with multidisciplinary artist Claire Barrow. Over the next six months, she moved between the studios of several emerging London fashion talents.<ref name="harpers" />

== Career ==
In 2018, Stark designed a custom piece for [[Beyoncé]] which appeared in the singer's [[music video]] for "[[Apeshit]]".<ref name="perfect"/> She subsequently designed another costume for Beyoncé's 2020 ''[[Black Is King]]'' musical film.<ref name="perfect"/> The endorsement of the superstar singer proved to be a great boost to Stark's career.<ref name="gee">{{cite news |last1=Gee |first1=Victor |title=Michaela Stark’s brand of inclusivity, backed by Beyoncé and Victoria’s Secret: how the couturier’s body-positive lingerie is challenging the fashion industry’s willingness to change |url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/fashion/fashion-news/article/3267055/michaela-starks-brand-inclusivity-backed-beyonce-and-victorias-secret-how-couturiers-body-positive |work=South China Morning Post |date=19 June 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Stark was invited to join a group of other artists in reimagining the [[Victoria's Secret Fashion Show]], which had been canceled since 2019.<ref name="vogue"/> She constructed couture looks for herself and two other [[plus-size model]]s: [[Jade O'Belle]] and Ceval.<ref name="vogue"/> Presenting the most ''avant garde'' looks in the filmed fashion show, some fans reacted negatively and organized a campaign of harassment during which she lost access to her social media accounts for some time.<ref name="vogue"/> 

That same year, she walked in the spring/summer show for [[Weinsanto]] in Paris, and launched her own line of [[ready-to-wear]] lingerie.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sangster |first1=Ella |title=Michaela Stark has launched a ready to wear collection |url=https://harpersbazaar.com.au/michaela-strak-launches-ready-to-wear/ |work=Harper's Bazaar Australia |date=November 2023}}</ref> She presented the collection, branded Panty, at [[Milan Fashion Week]].<ref name="collateral">{{cite news |last1=Massari |first1=Giorgia |title=Michaela Stark's Performance At Tate Britain |url=https://www.collater.al/en/performance-michaela-stark-tate-britain-london-art/ |work=Collateral |date=10 July 2024}}</ref>

In 2024 she [[performance art|performed]] at the [[Tate Britain]] as part of the ''[[Sargent and Fashion]]'' show.<ref name="collateral"/> Stark posed for hours in her signature tight-fitting lingerie, tangled in veil-like fabric, inside a crate meant to mimic the display boxes used in the exhibit.<ref>{{cite blog |last1=Pernet |first1=Diane |title=Redefining Beauty: Michaela Stark’s Revolutionary Corsetry and Fashion Performance at the Tate Britain |url=https://ashadedviewonfashion.com/2024/07/15/redefining-beauty-michaela-starks-revolutionary-corsetry-and-fashion-performance-at-the-tate-britain/ |work=A Shaded View on Fashion |date=15 July 2024}}</ref> The next year, her work was showcased, along with that of two other Brisbane artists, at the [[Institute of Modern Art]] in a show titled ''Confronting Femininity''.<ref name="bima"/> In 2026, several of Stark's pieces were featured in the New York [[Metropolitan Museum of Art|Metropolitan Museum]]'s annual [[Costume Institute]] exhibit, and custom [[mannequin]]s were constructed from scans of her body.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Noveck |first1=Jocelyn |title=Most fashion mannequins are about a size 2. The Met Gala exhibit is making room for diverse bodies |url=https://apnews.com/article/met-gala-mannequins-costume-art-body-positivity-832682a0821a15abf314f6a721ac9b68 |work=AP News |date=20 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Meltzer |first1=Marisa |title=From Molded Torsos to Corseted Curves, the State of the Body at The Met |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/style/story/met-gala-2026-costume-art-body |work=Vanity Fair |date=5 May 2026}}</ref> ''ArtNet'' identified her "Fat, not Fertile" piece as one of the "standouts" of the ''[[Costume Art]]'' show.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chen |first1=Min |title=Inside the Costume Institute Show Where Fashion Meets the Human Form |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/met-costume-institute-2026-highlights-2774886 |work=Artnet News |date=21 May 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Olivier has been diagnosed with ADHD.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Nascimento|first=Rafael|url=https://queer.ig.com.br/2023-08-09/demorou-muito-tempo-para-eu-fazer-as-pazes-comigo--diz-dante-olivier.html?Foto1|title='Demorou muito tempo para eu fazer as pazes comigo', diz Dante Olivier|date=August 9, 2023|accessdate=June 3, 2026|website=[[Internet Group|Portal iG]]|language=pt-BR|archive-date=January 18, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118133353/https://queer.ig.com.br/2023-08-09/demorou-muito-tempo-para-eu-fazer-as-pazes-comigo--diz-dante-olivier.html?Foto1|url-status=live|trans-title='It took me a long time to make peace with myself,' says Dante Olivier}}</ref>

Olivier discovered that he was a trans man when he was 16, starting his transition at 19.<ref name=":12"/> A bisexual man,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/fabia-oliveira/dante-olivier-revela-dificuldade-para-entender-sua-sexualidade|title=Dante Olivier revela dificuldade para entender sua sexualidade|date=October 10, 2023|accessdate=June 3, 2026|website=Metrópoles|language=pt-BR|archive-date=June 3, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260603172928/https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/fabia-oliveira/dante-olivier-revela-dificuldade-para-entender-sua-sexualidade|url-status=live|last=Oliveira|first=Fábia|trans-title=Dante Olivier reveals difficulty in understanding his sexuality}}</ref> he married his wife Victoria in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Vieira|url=https://midianinja.org/noivado-de-dante-olivier-e-vikki-subverte-logica-de-preconceito-e-exalta-os-afetos-lgbtqiapn/|title=Noivado de Dante Olivier e Vikki subverte lógica de preconceito e exalta os afetos LGBTQIAPN+|date=September 12, 2024|accessdate=June 3, 2026|website=[[Mídia Ninja|Mídia NINJA]]|language=pt-BR|first=Luiz|trans-title=Dante Olivier and Vikki's engagement subverts the logic of prejudice and celebrates LGBTQIAPN+ affections}}</ref>

'''Gustavo Adrián Tejera Capo''' (born 20 January 1988<ref name="ole">{{Cite web |date=2026-03-28 |title=Quién es Gustavo Tejera, el árbitro que dirigirá el debut de Boca en la Libertadores |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/boca-juniors/gustavo-tejera-arbitro-dirigira-debut-boca-libertadores_0_u5zuk9uzPe.html |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]] |language=es-AR}}</ref>) is a Uruguayan football referee who has been on the [[FIFA International Referees List]] since 2018.

== Career ==
Tejera was born in [[Montevideo]] in January 1988.<ref name="espn">{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/mundial/nota/_/id/16590238/gustavo-tejera-arbitro-uruguayo-2026-trayectoria-polemicas-perfil-estilo-anecdotas |access-date=2026-06-10 |title=Gustavo Tejera, el árbitro uruguayo en el Mundial 2026|work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> He became an active referee in 2014 by ascending to the [[Liga AUF Uruguaya]] in 2015.<ref name="espn"/> In 2018, Tejera earned his [[FIFA]] badge, making his international debut at [[Copa Sudamericana]] one year later and at [[Copa Libertadores]] in 2020.<ref name="ole"/><ref name="espn"/><ref name="clasicos"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=CONMEBOL confirmó los árbitros para el debut de Boca y River en las Copas |url=https://santafedeportivo.com/2026/03/28/conmebol-confirmo-los-arbitros-para-el-debut-de-boca-y-river-en-las-copas/ |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=Santa Fe Deportivo |language=es}}</ref>

At his home country's top-tier league, Tejera has overseen several ''[[Uruguayan Clásico|clásicos]]'' between [[Peñarol]] and [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]], including the final match of the [[2025 Liga AUF Uruguaya]] in November 2025, where Nacional were crowned champions.<ref name="clasicos">{{Cite news|title=Gustavo Tejera y su estilo: "La clave del arbitraje en general es tener una buena adaptabilidad"|url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/uruguay/nota/_/id/16003979/gustavo-tejera-estilo-arbitro-antecedentes-penarol-nacional-clasico |access-date=2026-06-10 |work=ESPN}}</ref> In the [[Supercopa Uruguaya]], Tejera was chosen for the [[2020 Supercopa Uruguaya|2020 edition]] game between [[Liverpool F.C. (Montevideo)|Liverpool]] and Nacional.<ref name="ole"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Díaz |first=Juan José |title=Segunda mirada: Tejera pésimo, Liverpool corajudo y el Chory fue el mejor de Nacional |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/segunda-mirada-tejera-pesimo-liverpool-corajudo-y-el-chory-fue-el-mejor-de-nacional-202022142030 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=[[El Observador (Uruguay)|El Observador]] |language=es-UY}}</ref>

Tejera has also taken part in international competitions of national teams, including [[CONMEBOL]] qualification matches for the [[FIFA World Cup]], the [[2023 FIFA U-17 World Cup]], and the [[2025 FIFA U-20 World Cup]]. 

He was appointed to the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] and, in April 2026, he was selected for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mujica |first=Lucas |date=2026-04-07 |title=“Yo prefiero no dialogar”: quién es Gustavo Tejera, el polémico árbitro del UC vs. Boca que fue criticado por Juan Tagle |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/yo-prefiero-no-dialogar-quien-es-gustavo-tejera-el-polemico-arbitro-del-uc-vs-boca-que-fue-criticado-por-juan-tagle/ |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=[[La Tercera]] |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/mundial/nota/_/id/16551513/se-confirmaron-los-arbitros-uruguayos-que-estaran-en-el-mundial-2026 |title=Se confirmaron los árbitros uruguayos que estarán en el Mundial 2026|access-date=2026-06-10 |website=www.espn.com.ar}}</ref> Tejera took charge of the group stage match between [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] and [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]]. He was also appointed to the round of 32 knockout match between [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] and [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]]. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramírez |first=Gabriel |last2=USA |first2=AS |date=2026-07-03 |title=Who is Gustavo Tejera, the referee for Australia vs Egypt in the round of 32 at the 2026 World Cup? |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/who-is-gustavo-tejera-the-referee-for-australia-vs-egypt-in-the-round-of-32-at-the-2026-world-cup-f202607-n/ |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=AS USA |language=en-us}}</ref>

Aside from his refereeing career, Tejera is an [[insurance broker]] and has two children.<ref name="espn"/>

'''Austin Sellinger''' (born April 19, 1998), known professionally as '''Roe Kapara''', is an American singer. His music incorporates elements of [[psychedelic rock]] and [[indie pop]], and is known for incorporating a macabre, otherworldly, and surreal aesthetic.

==Biography==
Kapara was born Austin Sellinger in St. Louis, and was raised in the [[Catholic Church]] in Missouri. His Catholic heritage went on to inspire his song "Preacher", the featured song on his first EP.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bronson |first=Kevin |date=2023-11-06 |title=Ears Wide Open: Roe Kapara |url=https://buzzbands.la/2023/11/05/ears-wide-open-roe-kapara/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=buzzbands.la |language=en}}</ref>

He spent some time living in Nashville, but moved to [[Los Angeles]] just before the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TREES {{!}} Roe Kapara |url=https://2000trees.co.uk/line-up/roe-kapara#:~:text=%E2%80%9CNobody%20was%20born%20cool,%E2%80%9D,online%20and%20build%20a%20community. |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=2000trees.co.uk |archive-date=June 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622111341/https://2000trees.co.uk/line-up/roe-kapara#:~:text=%E2%80%9CNobody%20was%20born%20cool,%E2%80%9D,online%20and%20build%20a%20community. |url-status=live }}</ref> During this time before the pandemic, he performed a lot of live shows, including many in which he opened for comedians.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Morton |first=Ken |date=2023-03-15 |title=Introducing Roe Kapara: Employment Cost and Beyond |url=https://highwiredaze.com/2023/03/14/roekaparaint1/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Highwire Daze |language=en-US |archive-date=March 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312164503/https://highwiredaze.com/2023/03/14/roekaparaint1/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During the pandemic, he began shifting to building an online presence with his songs,<ref name=":0" /> such as "Waiting", "Baby Blue", "I Wanted You", and "Past Grow" and soon went viral for his 2021 single "Employment Cost".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roe Kapara |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/roe-kapara/id1577026423?i=1000535034942 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-US}}</ref>

He signed with [[Epitaph Records]] in 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Connection |first=Music |date=2023-02-06 |title=Roe Kapara Signs to Epitaph Records - Music Connection Magazine |url=https://www.musicconnection.com/roe-kapara-signs-to-epitaph-records/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=www.musicconnection.com |language=en-US |archive-date=January 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124020837/https://www.musicconnection.com/roe-kapara-signs-to-epitaph-records/ |url-status=live }}</ref> partially inspired by his close friend and musical collaborator [[Dolo Tonight]] also signing with Epitaph.<ref name=":0" /> He went on to collaborate with Dolo for their single "Fake My Death". that same year,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Vigil |first=Dom |date=2023-06-07 |title=Dolo Tonight & Roe Kapara Share New Single, "Fake My Death" |url=https://preludepress.com/news/2023/06/07/dolo-tonight-roe-kapara-fake-my-death/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |language=en-US |archive-date=August 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250806205745/https://preludepress.com/news/2023/06/07/dolo-tonight-roe-kapara-fake-my-death/ |url-status=live }}</ref> among numerous other singles he created. He released his first EP, ''I Hope Hell Isn't Real'', in 2023<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Roe Kapara Makes Stellar Debut On 'I Hope Hell Isn't Real' EP [Q&A] {{!}} THE NOISE |url=http://www.onestowatch.com/en/blog/roe-kapara-makes-stellar-debut-on-i-hope-hell-isnt-real-ep-qa-the-noise |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Ones to Watch |language=en |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206025100/https://www.onestowatch.com/en/blog/roe-kapara-makes-stellar-debut-on-i-hope-hell-isnt-real-ep-qa-the-noise |url-status=live }}</ref> and followed it up with ''Big Cigars and Satin Shorts'' in 2024. He also performed at [[2000trees]] in 2024.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-08-23 |title=Roe Kapara releases second EP, plus new video for Hate Myself |url=https://www.kerrang.com/roe-kapara-releases-second-ep-plus-new-video-for-hate-myself |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Kerrang! |language=en |archive-date=July 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725043948/https://www.kerrang.com/roe-kapara-releases-second-ep-plus-new-video-for-hate-myself |url-status=live }}</ref>

He draws inspiration from 90s movies and movies in general when writing his songs.<ref name=":2" />

His music and the accompanying videos emphasize otherworldly, bizarre, surreal, and macabre imagery and presentation,<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Rise Of Indie Rockstar Roe Kapara |url=https://idobi.com/video/the-rise-of-indie-rockstar-roe-kapara/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=idobi |language=en-US |archive-date=January 22, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122185436/https://idobi.com/video/the-rise-of-indie-rockstar-roe-kapara/ |url-status=live }}</ref> for example the [[stop motion]] animation utilized in the music video to his 2023 single "The Dead Come Talking".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Major |first=Michael |date=2023-09-14 |title=Roe Kapara Shares New Track 'The Dead Come Talking' |url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/bwwmusic/article/Roe-Kapara-Shares-New-Track-The-Dead-Come-Talking-20230914 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=BroadwayWorld.com |language=en}}</ref> His 2026 single "Crying on Vacation", however, leaned into [[surf rock]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Logan |first=Tate |date=2026-06-10 |title=Roe Kapara Is "Crying On Vacation" In New Track |url=https://idobi.org/news/roe-kapara-is-crying-on-vacation-in-new-track/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=idobi |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Joseph Barnett Jr.'''<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2013 |title=Wilkinsburg Rap Artist Who Signed $3 Million Contract Jailed, Faces Drug Charges |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/wilkinsburg-rap-artist-jailed-faces-drug-charges/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> (born May 6, 1992),<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Deitch |first=Charlie |date=August 10, 2016 |title=Pittsburgh rapper Hardo’s long walk to redemption |url=https://www.pghcitypaper.com/arts-entertainment-2/pittsburgh-rapper-hardos-long-walk-to-redemption-1942779/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=Pittsburgh City Paper |language=en-US}}</ref> known professionally as '''Hardo''', is an American rapper. He is best known for his collaborations with other Pittsburgh-based rappers such as [[Jimmy Wopo]], [[Mac Miller]], and [[Wiz Khalifa]].

==Early life==
Barnett was born on May 6, 1992, in [[Wilkinsburg, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=":0" /> Barnett attended [[Taylor Allderdice High School]], where he became friends with rapper and future collaborator, [[Mac Miller]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goddard |first=Kevin |date=October 10, 2015 |title=Mac Miller Affiliated Rapper, Hardo, Busted With Heroin |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/15182-mac-miller-affiliated-rapper-hardo-busted-with-heroin-news |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2009, Barnett started making music with his classmate, Mac Miller.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Kramer |first=Kyle |date=November 3, 2014 |title=Listen to "Trapnati," Pittsburgh Rapper Hardo's First Single Since His Release from Prison |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/pittsburgh-rapper-hardo-trapnati-out-of-prison/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=VICE |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2011, he released his breakout song "Cut Throat".<ref name=":3" />

After being released from jail in 2014, Barnett released the single "Trapnati", which would be the title song for his mixtape.<ref name=":3" /> In November 2015, he released the [[Extended play|EP]] "Drug Related", which had features from [[Shy Glizzy]], [[Trae tha Truth]], and Jimmy Wopo, as well as production from [[Metro Boomin]], [[Sonny Digital]], and more.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Joe |date=November 18, 2015 |title=Hardo - Drug Related [EP] |url=http://onsmash.com/music/hardo-drug-related-ep/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=OnSMASH |language=en}}</ref>

In March 2016, Barnett released the single "Blasphemy", which rapper [[21 Savage]] was featured on.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ivey |first=Justin |date=March 16, 2016 |title=Hardo Collaborates With 21 Savage on "Blasphemy" |url=https://www.xxlmag.com/hardo-21-savage-blasphemy/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=XXL Mag |language=en}}</ref> In late 2016, he released a collaborative mixtape with [[Jimmy Wopo]], with features from 21 Savage and [[Wiz Khalifa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Pittsburgh rapper Jimmy Wopo joins the million club |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/ae/music/2016/12/22/pittsburgh-rapper-jimmy-wopo-joins-the-million-club/stories/201612220010 |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref> In late-2016, he released the single "Today's a Good Day", featuring Wiz Khalifa and Jimmy Wopo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=M. |first=Emmanuel C. |date=October 18, 2017 |title=Hardo, Jimmy Wopo and Wiz Khalifa's ''Today's a Good Day'' Video |url=https://www.xxlmag.com/hardo-jimmy-wopo-wiz-khalifa-todays-a-good-day-video/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=XXL Mag |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
===Legal issues===
In 2009, Barnett was arrested for the first time, in [[New Kensington, Pennsylvania]], on charges of [[home invasion]]. In 2010, he was arrested for possession of heroin, and was sentenced to probation.<ref name=":0" /> In March 2010, he was arrested once again for possession of heroin with the intent to distribute.

In August 2013, Barnett was [[Traffic stop|pulled over]] for failing to stop at a stop sign,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2013 |title=Wilkinsburg rapper Hardo held for trial on felony drug charge |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/local/east/2013/12/05/rapper-hardo-held-for-trial-on-felony-drug-charge/stories/201312050278 |access-date=June 15, 2026 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref> when police would found 250 stamp-bags containing heroin,<ref name=":0" /> leading to Barnett making an attempt to flee, however he was tackled by an officer, he was arrested and charged with heroin possession with the intent to distribute, [[resisting arrest]], and attempt to flee from a crime scene. He was sent the [[Allegheny County Jail]], and his bond was set at [[United States dollar|$]]25,000.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

'''Brisa Silva Bracchi''' (born 20 December 1997) is a Brazilian politician and human rights activist. A member of the [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]], she has served as a city councillor on the [[Municipal Chamber of Natal]] since 2020. In 2022, Bracchi was chosen as Natal's "outstanding parliamentarian", in recognition of her work introducing and passing inclusive laws in the city.

== Early life and education ==
Bracchi was born on 20 December 1997 in [[Natal, Rio Grande do Norte|Natal]], the capital of [[Rio Grande do Norte]], a state in the [[Northeast Region, Brazil|Northeast Region]] of [[Brazil]]. In 2015, while in secondary school, she was active in student politics, being elected to serve as director of women for the [[Brazilian Union of Secondary School Students]]. Bracchi took part in the [[2016 student protests in Brazil|2016 student protests]], a series of demonstrations and school occupations against proposed changes to education by the government of then-[[President of Brazil]], [[Michel Temer]], including the proposed [[New Brazilian secondary education|new Brazilian secondary education system]] and the [[Constitutional Amendment of the Public Expenditure Cap]], which would limit government funding in education.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Brisa Bracchi |url=https://www.cmnat.rn.gov.br/vereadores/57 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421024101/https://www.cmnat.rn.gov.br/vereadores/57 |archive-date=21 April 2024 |access-date=24 June 2026 |work=[[Municipal Chamber of Natal|Câmara Municipal de Natal]] |language=pt }}</ref>

After completing secondary school, Bracchi started studying history at the [[Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte]]. During her time at university, she served as the general coordinator of the José Silton Pereira Central Student Directory between 2018 and 2019; Bracchi was also elected as the general secretary of [[State Union of Students]], a student organisation associated with the [[National Union of Students (Brazil)|National Union of Students]], for Rio Grande do Norte.<ref name=":0" />

After graduating from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte, Bracchi subsequently obtained a second degree, in environmental studies, from the [[Federal Institute of Rio Grande do Norte]].<ref name=":0" />

== Political career ==
At the age of 18, Bracchi joined the Workers' Party, a centre-left national political party. She self-identified with the party's democratic socialist bloc. When she was 21, Bracchi was elected general secretary of the Workers' Party's Natal Municipal Executive; three years later, she was named the party's state secretary for women.<ref name=":0" />

Following the [[2020 Brazilian municipal elections|2020 municipal elections]], Bracchi was elected to the Municipal Chamber of Natal; she had run on a portfolio of promoting culture, education, and [[LGBTQ rights in Brazil|LGBTQ]] and [[Indigenous rights in Brazil|indigenous rights]]; she also stated she would seek to legalise [[Medical cannabis|medicinal cannabis]]. In 2021, Bracchi became leader of the chamber's opposition bloc.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=26 February 2021 |title=Brisa Bracchi é nova líder da bancada de oposição na Câmara de Natal |trans-title=Brisa Bracchi is the new leader of the opposition bloc on Natal City Council |url=https://tribunadonorte.com.br/natal/brisa-bracchi-e-nova-lider-da-bancada-de-oposicao-na-camara-de-natal/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421024103/https://tribunadonorte.com.br/natal/brisa-bracchi-e-nova-lider-da-bancada-de-oposicao-na-camara-de-natal/ |archive-date=21 April 2024 |access-date=24 June 2026 |work=Tribuna do Norte |language=pt }}</ref>

As a result of the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil|COVID-19 pandemic]], Bracchi's called for the creation of the Municipal Emergency Basic Income Programme to address inequalities in accessing healthcare among disadvantaged communities in Natal. Bracchi also successfully passed the Municipal Policy for Comprehensive Health of the LGBTI+ Population, which sought to ensure Basic Health Units were better able to serve LGBTQ+ patients, such as through knowledge and access to [[transgender health care]]. Following the conclusion of Bracchi's first year in office, she was identified by the Municipal Chamber as being the "most productive" council member.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last1=Melo |first1=Cecília |last2=Macedo |first2=Nathallya |date=25 June 2022 |title=Leis e outras medidas que protegem a população LGBT+ potiguar são destaques positivos |trans-title=Laws and other measures protecting the LGBT+ population of Rio Grande do Norte are positive highlights |url=https://agorarn.com.br/ultimas/leis-e-outras-medidas-que-protegem-a-populacao-lgbt-potiguar-sao-destaques-positivos/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926032455/https://agorarn.com.br/ultimas/leis-e-outras-medidas-que-protegem-a-populacao-lgbt-potiguar-sao-destaques-positivos/ |archive-date=26 September 2025 |access-date=24 June 2026 |work=Agora RN |language=pt}}</ref>

In 2022, Bracchi authored a bill that recognised and commemorated [[Celebrate Bisexuality Day]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pazatto |first=Deivid |date=16 March 2022 |title=Lei que reconhece o "Dia da '''Jeffrey William Chad Nippard''' (born October 6, 1990) is a Canadian [[YouTuber]] and [[Bodybuilding|bodybuilder]]. He is one of the leading figures of the science-based lifting movement, which uses research to reduce injury and maximize results in opposition to pseudoscientific bodybuilding techniques, sometimes called "[[wiktionary:broscience|broscience]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeff Nippard Fitness {{!}} Science-Based Bodybuilding |url=https://jeffnippard.com/ |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=Jeff Nippard Fitness |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jeffrey William Chad Nippard<ref name="conv">{{Cite web |title=Spring Convocation 2012 |url=https://www.mun.ca/convocation/media/production/convocation/media-library/previous/Spring_2012_SJ.pdf |access-date=September 29, 2026 |website=Memorial University of Newfoundland}}</ref> was born on October 6, 1990, in [[Grand Falls-Windsor]], [[Newfoundland and Labrador]].<ref name="triumphs">{{Cite web |date=2014-07-20 |title=Grand Falls-Windsor Native Talks About his Recent Bodybuilding Triumphs in California |url=https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/audio/1.2713221 |access-date=August 9, 2026 |website=CBC}}</ref> He graduated from the [[Memorial University of Newfoundland]] with a degree in biochemistry.<ref name="chin"/>

==Career==
Nippard performed in his first bodybuilding show when he was nineteen. In 2012, he was awarded Mr. Junior Canada.<ref name="volt">{{Cite web |date=December 28, 2016 |title=Jeff Nippard Got Boulder Shoulders |url=https://fitnessvolt.com/5691/jeff-nippard-got-boulder-shoulders/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Fitness Volt |language=en-US}}</ref> Nippard created his YouTube channel in 2014. He had been consistently going to the gym since 2005, although, before discovering science-based lifting in 2014, he had been an adherent to the broscience movement. Nippard's early videos were based around his workouts, later shifting to presenting research in a digestible way.<ref name="chin"/>

In 2021, Nippard launched MacroFactor, a premium app that tracked nutrients. By this time, he had been selling training programs on his website.<ref name="chin"/> In October 2024, Nippard was involved in an altercation with bodybuilder Mike Van Wyck at a [[Burlington, Ontario]], gym that resulted in Van Wyck being charged with two counts of assault after hitting Nippard and his cameraman. The confrontation was due to Van Wyck uploading a video titled "Science Based Scammers" and Nippard making video in response that refuted Van Wyck's claims.<ref name="arnold">{{Cite web |last=Arnold |first=Chris |date=October 28, 2024 |title=Viral assault at Halton gym leads to charges for Drake's ex-bodyguard |url=https://www.miltontoday.ca/local-news/viral-assault-at-halton-gym-leads-to-charges-for-drakes-ex-bodyguard-9719059 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=MiltonToday.ca |language=en}}</ref><ref name="leaked">{{Cite web |last=Arnold |first=Chris |date=October 31, 2024 |title=Leaked video shows full viral Halton gym assault |url=https://www.oakvillenews.org/local-news/leaked-video-shows-full-viral-halton-gym-assault-9737332 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Oakville News |language=en}}</ref>

In December 2024, Nippard published an instructional book, ''The Muscle Ladder: Get Jacked Using Science''. In September 2025, Nippard revealed the Muscle Lab, a {{cvt|4000|sqft|sqm}}, $3 million dollar research facility in [[Oakville, Ontario]]. He had been working on the project for two years with design studio Nivek Remas and planned to used it as a studio where he would also conduct experiments that would get peer reviewed and published in science journals.<ref name="chin">{{Cite web |last=Chin |first=Tyler |date=December 15, 2025 |title=How Jeff Nippard Became the Face (and Body) of Science-Based Lifting |url=https://www.gq.com/story/how-jeff-nippard-became-the-face-and-body-of-science-based-lifting |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=GQ |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="kryger">{{Cite web |last=Kryger |first=Kelsey |date=2025-09-10 |title=Jeff Nippard Says He Just Built the ‘Most Scientific Gym On the Planet’ |url=https://www.mensfitness.com/news/jeff-nippard-says-he-just-built-the-most-scientific-gym-on-the-planet |access-date=August 9, 2026 |website=Men's Fitness}}</ref><ref name="aksich">{{Cite web |last=Aksich |first=Caroline |date=January 7, 2026 |title=Five of the Toronto’s most hard-core new fitness clubs |url=https://torontolife.com/city/five-of-the-torontos-most-hard-core-new-fitness-clubs/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Toronto Life |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2016, Nippard began dating fellow fitness influencer Stephanie Buttermore.<ref name="lacroix">{{Cite news |last=LaCroix |first=Emy |date=March 7, 2026 |title=Why Stephanie Buttermore Quit YouTube 2 Years Before Her Death |url=https://parade.com/news/why-stephanie-buttermore-quit-youtube-2-years-before-her-death-jeff-nippard-fiancee-dies |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260309191316/https://parade.com/news/why-stephanie-buttermore-quit-youtube-2-years-before-her-death-jeff-nippard-fiancee-dies |archive-date=2026-03-09 |access-date=2026-08-09 |work=Parade |language=en}}</ref> Buttermore had a PhD in pathology and cell biology and researched ovarian cancer.<ref name="chinman">{{Cite web |last=Chinman |first=Luke |date=2026-04-28 |title=Fiancé of Fitness Influencer Stephanie Buttermore Breaks Silence After Her Death at 36 |url=https://people.com/fiance-of-fitness-influencer-stephanie-buttermore-breaks-silence-after-her-death-at-36-11960793 |access-date=August 9, 2026 |website=People.com}}</ref> They became engaged in October 2022. Buttermore died on March 6, 2026.<ref name="albaroudi">{{Cite web |last=AlBaroudi |first=Wajih |date=2026-03-07 |title=Stephanie Buttermore cause of death: What we know about influencer |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/pop-culture/2026/03/07/stephanie-buttermore-cause-of-death-fitness-influencer/89035983007/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=For The Win |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="murray">{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Tom |date=March 7, 2026 |title=Stephanie Buttermore, influencer fiancée of YouTube star Jeff Nippard, dies aged 36 |url=https://www.the-independent.com/life-style/stephanie-buttermore-death-cause-jeff-nippard-b2933932.html |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref name="flam">{{Cite news |last=Flam |first=Charna |date=2026-03-07 |title=Fitness Influencer Stephanie Buttermore Dies at 36, Fiancé Jeff Nippard Announces |url=https://people.com/fitness-influencer-stephanie-buttermore-dies-at-36-fiance-jeff-nippard-announces-11921523 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312085803/https://people.com/fitness-influencer-stephanie-buttermore-dies-at-36-fiance-jeff-nippard-announces-11921523 |archive-date=2026-03-12 |access-date=2026-08-09 |work=People.com}}</ref> After, Nippard struggled with depression and took time off social media.<ref name="parent">{{Cite web |last=Parent |first=Tabitha |date=2026-05-27 |title=Fiancé of Late Fitness Influencer Stephanie Buttermore Candidly Details Grappling with 'Bad' Depression Following Her Death |url=https://people.com/fiance-of-late-fitness-influencer-details-bad-depression-following-her-death-11984523 |access-date=August 9, 2026 |website=People.com}}</ref>
